title: Implement install-home resolution with graceful disablement
description:
## Objective
Implement `plugin/server/install-home.ts` to resolve `<install home>` from the registered directory-plugin path, validate it using read-only `install.json`, fall back to `~/.paseo-bm`, and return a readable disabled reason instead of throwing.

## Context
The plugin bundle has no reliable cwd or `import.meta.url`; the registered Paseo path is the authority and must support custom `--home` installations.

## Scope
In scope:
- Read `config.plugins["paseo-bm"].path`, move up two levels, and validate readable `install.json`/schemaVersion.
- Fall back to `~/.paseo-bm` only as specified.
- Return `null` plus a user-readable reason when unavailable.
- Five approved resolution tests.
Out of scope:
- Creating, repairing, or writing `install.json`; guessing other paths; trace-store I/O.

## Components Touched
- `plugin/server/install-home.ts` — resolver.
- Focused server tests with fake config and fake home.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- WP-201 Dashboard contract/error-code task must be complete for approved notices/codes.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- `install.json` is the only file read here and is never modified.
- Standard and non-default `--home` registrations must both resolve successfully.
- Missing `install.json`, missing plugin config, and `config.get()` errors return disabled state without throwing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Standard registered path resolves correctly.
- A non-default home resolves correctly.
- Missing `install.json`, absent `plugins.paseo-bm`, and config errors each return `null` with a readable reason and do not throw.
- No test observes a filesystem write.

## Primary Proof
Focused Vitest resolver tests against fake config and temporary homes plus plugin typecheck.

## Reversibility
Local server module; revert restores tracing-disabled behavior without modifying user data.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-dashboard-implementation-plan.md#WP-202
Requirements: REQ-053(b), REQ-049(d)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-dashboard.md §3.1 and docs/design/paseo-bm.md errata bm-dnc
close_reason: Added plugin/server/install-home.ts: resolveInstallHome() reads config.plugins['paseo-bm'].path via the SDK, takes the install home two levels up (<home>/plugin/<version>), confirms it with a read-only install.json whose schemaVersion must be <= 1, otherwise falls back to ~/.paseo-bm, and returns { home: null, reason } instead of throwing. A registered path that is a developer checkout falls through to the default home rather than disabling tracing. Exported installHomeFromPluginPath and confirmInstallHome so both steps are testable on their own. Proof: test/plugin-install-home.test.ts (16 tests) covers the five approved cases — standard path, non-default --home, missing install.json everywhere, absent plugins.paseo-bm (both with and without a usable default home), and config.get() throwing — plus a schemaVersion-too-new refusal, broken JSON, missing schemaVersion, and an assertion that the only path read is <home>/install.json, which is also how it proves no write happens (the injected fs fake exposes no write function). Note: plugin/tsconfig.json needed "types": ["react", "node"] because the server entry is the first payload module to use node:path; the client/shared no-node import boundary is still enforced by plugin-structure.test.ts (63 tests green). typecheck:plugin + lint clean.

title: WP-203: Build the durable trace store
description:
## Purpose
Create the first plugin-owned disk-write boundary: a versioned, append-only, bounded trace store under `<install home>/traces/`.

## Scope
Shared no-follow path protection and workspace mutexes, safe append/read/meta/size operations, schema compatibility, permissions, malformed-line tolerance, and negative containment evidence.

## Success Criteria
- Both WP-203 child tasks close with all no-follow, concurrency, durability, permission, and schema tests passing.
- No module outside `trace-store.ts` constructs writable trace-store paths.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-dashboard-implementation-plan.md#WP-203
Requirements: REQ-048(c), REQ-049(a), REQ-053(a)(b)(c), REQ-055(a)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-dashboard.md §§3.2–3.4, 3.6, 3.8; docs/adr/ADR-007-dashboard-trace-store.md
close_reason: Join: both children closed. bm-wp-203-4vj.1 delivered the shared no-follow path guard (lstat every component, O_NOFOLLOW, O_EXCL temp files, 0700/0600) and the in-process mutex keyed by workspaceId with a 5 s wait and a distinguishable TraceStoreLockTimeout; .2 delivered append/read/dedupe/metadata/sizing on top of it, including tolerant line skipping and the never-write rule for a newer schema. Combined proof: 52 tests across plugin-trace-store-guard (29) and plugin-trace-store (23) on real temp filesystems, including symlink refusal at four placements with targets asserted unchanged, a truncated-final-line survival case, and a barrier test for append racing a rewrite. One durable trace-store lifecycle, one containment boundary.

title: Implement the shared no-follow path guard and workspace mutex
description:
## Objective
Implement in `plugin/server/trace-store.ts` the sole writable-path resolver and the in-process asynchronous mutex keyed by `workspaceId` required by Dashboard Design §3.8.

## Context
All append, delete, and reassign mutations run in one plugin-server process. They must share one containment and serialization mechanism so symlinks cannot escape the store and same-workspace mutations cannot interleave.

## Scope
In scope:
- Validate `workspaceId` with `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$`, excluding `.` and `..`.
- Resolve beneath `<install home>/traces`, `lstat` every component, reject every symlink, use `O_NOFOLLOW`; temporary files use `O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW` in the destination directory.
- Async mutex keyed by workspace id covering all store mutations; collector wait limit is the designed default 5 seconds.
- Tests for symlinks at `traces/`, workspace directory, monthly file, and temporary file, and for mutex ordering/timeouts.
Out of scope:
- Trace record parsing/storage behavior, RPC handlers, UI confirmation, or filesystem locking across processes.

## Components Touched
- `plugin/server/trace-store.ts` — shared path and mutex primitives.
- Trace-store security/concurrency tests under `test/`.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- WP-201 contract task supplies `E_TRACE_STORE_UNWRITABLE`.
- WP-202 resolver supplies the validated install home.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Collector and RPC handlers share one plugin-server process; do not add a file lock.
- Reads do not acquire the mutex.
- No other module may construct writable trace-store paths directly.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Prefix checks alone are insufficient; every existing path component must be checked without following symlinks.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All four symlink placements fail with `E_TRACE_STORE_UNWRITABLE` before mutation, and each symlink target remains byte-identical.
- Same-workspace mutations serialize; different workspace ids can proceed independently.
- Timeout behavior is observable to callers and does not leave the mutex held.
- Temporary creation flags and same-directory placement match Design §3.8 on macOS and Linux.

## Primary Proof
Focused Vitest path-attack and barrier-controlled mutex tests on temporary filesystems, plus plugin typecheck.

## Reversibility
Local infrastructure; revert disables dependent store work. No existing user store exists before this feature.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-dashboard-implementation-plan.md#WP-203
Requirements: REQ-047, REQ-053(b)(c), REQ-054(d), REQ-057(g)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-dashboard.md §3.8; docs/adr/ADR-007-dashboard-trace-store.md decisions 3, 5, 7
close_reason: Added plugin/server/trace-store.ts primitives per Design §3.8. Path guard: assertWorkspaceId (^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$, with . and .. excluded explicitly), storePath (absolute store dir, per-segment traversal refusal, prefix containment, then no-follow), assertNoSymlinkOnPath (lstat every existing component from the install home down, never following), ensureStoreDir (symlink check before AND after mkdir 0700 to close the appear-between-check-and-mkdir window), openStoreFileForAppend with O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_APPEND|O_NOFOLLOW at 0600, createStoreTempFile with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW in the destination directory so rename stays on one filesystem. Lock: withWorkspaceLock, one async chain per workspaceId, reads take nothing; TraceStoreLockTimeout (a distinct subclass of DashboardError so the collector can tell busy from broken) after the designed 5000 ms default; a timed-out waiter releases its slot so the queue keeps draining and the lock is never left held; idle workspaces are dropped from the map. Proof: test/plugin-trace-store-guard.test.ts (29 tests) on a real temp filesystem — symlink refused at all four placements (traces/, workspace dir, monthly file, temp file) with the symlink TARGET asserted byte-identical afterwards, O_NOFOLLOW refusal even when a stale path reaches open(), O_EXCL refusal of a pre-existing temp file, modes asserted 0700/0600, id validation table, traversal segments rejected, plus mutex tests for same-workspace serialisation (barrier-controlled), cross-workspace independence, timeout with queue still draining, release on throw, and id validation before acquiring. typecheck:plugin + lint clean.

title: Implement append-only trace persistence, reading, and sizing
description:
## Objective
Implement version-1 trace-store creation, safe append, tolerant read, workspace metadata, deduplication, and byte/trace sizing under `<install home>/traces/`.

## Context
Completed agent turns must survive plugin reload, daemon restart, and agent deletion while tracing failures never disrupt an agent turn.

## Scope
In scope:
- Store/root/workspace `meta.json`, monthly `events-YYYYMM.jsonl`, one redacted record per line.
- `O_APPEND`, one newline-terminated write, `fsync`, dedupe by `(agentId, turnId)` keeping latest `at`.
- Newest-to-oldest reads with page limit 50, malformed/truncated final-line skipping and `skippedLines`, mtime+size cache, `stat` sizing.
- `0700` directories, `0600` metadata/monthly/temp files, text caps from Design §3.3.
- Newer schema: limited read plus notice, never write.
Out of scope:
- Collector hook registration, trace grouping, delete/reassign algorithms, UI, or backfill from old timelines.

## Components Touched
- `plugin/server/trace-store.ts` — store operations built only on the shared guard/mutex.
- Trace-store unit tests under `test/`.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- Shared no-follow path guard and mutex task must be complete.
- WP-201 contract/schema task and WP-202 install-home resolver must be complete.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Append is the normal mutation; deletion is the only later rewrite path.
- Errors including ENOSPC/permission/newer schema are logged once and contained, never thrown out of agent-hook callers.
- Before this version no store exists; no historical backfill is attempted.

## Risks / Gotchas
- A process may die after a partial final write; completed prior lines must remain usable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Round-trip, duplicate, malformed line, truncated final line, multiple month, cache, cap, and exact `stat` sizing tests pass.
- Newer schema is limited-read/no-write; equal/older supported schemas behave as designed.
- ENOSPC and permission failures are contained and logged.
- Permissions are `0700` for store/workspace directories and `0600` for metadata, monthly, and temporary files.
- Barrier test proves append serialized with another mutation loses and duplicates no record.

## Primary Proof
Focused Vitest filesystem suite on temporary homes plus plugin typecheck.

## Reversibility
Code is revertible; created user data is retained and can later be removed only through the approved user deletion flow. Downgrade containment is limited read/no-write for unknown newer schema.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-dashboard-implementation-plan.md#WP-203
Requirements: REQ-048(c), REQ-049(a), REQ-053(a)(b)(c), REQ-055(a)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-dashboard.md §§3.2–3.4, 3.6, 3.8; docs/adr/ADR-007-dashboard-trace-store.md decisions 1–5, 7–8

title: Implement tolerant BM report and review parsing
description:
## Objective
Implement `plugin/server/bm-report.ts` to find and normalize every `BM-REPORT` and `BM-REVIEW` block in text while remaining backward compatible and preserving unread fields.

## Context
Role instructions now have two consumers: Manager and Dashboard. Parser tolerance prevents an additive or partially missing report format from breaking historical traces.

## Scope
In scope:
- Fenced/unfenced blocks, case-insensitive keys, arbitrary order, missing/unknown fields, multiple blocks, quoted repeats.
- `unparsedFields`, null for absent/unread values, `none`/empty as absence.
- Bead ids split on comma/whitespace and filtered to valid ids.
- Deduplicate quoted reports using the designed `(agentId, phase, requestId, at)` key.
- Current, prior, and missing/additional-field fixtures for reports and reviews.
Out of scope:
- Changing role report format, trace grouping, bead-store lookup, or workflow inference.

## Components Touched
- `plugin/server/bm-report.ts` — parser/normalizer.
- Parser fixture tests under `test/`.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- WP-201 shared normalized report/review types must be complete.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Unknown fields are retained rather than rejected.
- Any future role-format change must update this parser in the same change while keeping the preceding fixture green.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Tests cover BM-REVIEW, full block, missing field, unknown field, multiple blocks, quoted block, key case variation, `none`, mixed id separators, and prior-instruction format.
- Empty/`none` values normalize to absence rather than string `"none"`.
- Prior-format compatibility stays green when the current fixture changes.

## Primary Proof
Focused Vitest parser compatibility suite plus plugin typecheck.

## Reversibility
Local pure parser; revert restores prior interpretation without modifying persisted source lines.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-dashboard-implementation-plan.md#WP-204
Requirements: REQ-042(c), REQ-044(b), REQ-050(a)(b)(c)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-dashboard.md §6 and §15; plugin/roles/worker.md Reporting
close_reason: Added plugin/server/bm-report.ts: parseReports/parseReviews read every block in a message, fenced or unfenced, quoted or not; keys are normalised case- and separator-insensitively (requestId == request_id == REQUESTID) so key case and order do not matter; unknown keys are kept in unparsedFields instead of rejecting the block; none/-/n\a/empty normalise to null absence rather than the string 'none'; bead ids split on comma/semicolon/whitespace, strip surrounding punctuation and backticks, de-duplicate and are filtered by a bead-id pattern so prose never becomes an id; parseGuardrail reads batch/reviews/polish/total/userAllowedExtra with every counter independently nullable and keeps the raw text for the observed-vs-claimed comparison; quoted repeats are dropped on the designed (agentId, phase, requestId, at) key; a block ends at prose so it cannot swallow the rest of a message; BM-REVIEW also reads a verdict carried on the marker line (BM-REVIEW STOPPED from bm-wq6); looksLikeReport distinguishes a report from a user request that merely mentions the word. Proof: test/plugin-bm-report.test.ts (29 tests) covering all ten required fixtures — BM-REVIEW, full current block, missing field, unknown field, multiple blocks, quoted block counted once, key case variation, none normalisation, mixed id separators, and a PRIOR_FORMAT fixture (unfenced, snake_case, no tier) that is the REQ-050b compatibility guard. typecheck:plugin + lint clean.

title: Implement the non-blocking redacted turn collector
description:
## Objective
Implement `plugin/server/collector.ts` and server registration for `agent.turn_started`/`agent.turn_ended`, collecting only `bm-*` agents, redacting before persistence, and containing all failures.

## Context
The collector is on the live agent path and creates the durable history consumed by trace reconstruction. It must never turn trace-store failure into agent failure.

## Scope
In scope:
- Track starts, handle ended outcomes `completed`/`failed`/`canceled`, and tolerate missing start.
- Filter provider ids beginning `bm-`; build the approved record, parse reports/reviews, update changed workspace metadata, redact/truncate before store append.
- If hook items lack timestamps, use the approved one-call `timeline.refetch` window fallback.
- Missing hooks become a logged no-op; store/mutex timeout errors are swallowed and logged.
- Tests and recorded p95 benchmark for the largest allowed record.
Out of scope:
- Trace grouping/read RPCs, non-BM agents, polling/background loops, or writing anywhere except through trace-store.

## Components Touched
- `plugin/server/collector.ts` — hooks and record assembly.
- `plugin/index.server.ts` — collector registration.
- Collector tests/benchmark under `test/`.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- WP-203 durable store must be complete.
- WP-204 report/review parser must be complete.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Redaction occurs before any disk write; do not persist env or agent config.
- Collector waits on the per-workspace mutex; after the designed 5-second limit it drops the turn and logs rather than blocking the agent.
- No network, agent creation/control, prompt sending, or workspace writes.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Any exception escaping the hook can affect a real agent turn.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Tests cover BM-only filtering, all three outcomes, missing hook, missing start, timestamp-present and timestamp-absent/refetch inputs, write failure, and mutex timeout.
- Disk assertion proves secrets are redacted before append.
- Recorded benchmark environment and p95 for maximum record is under 50 ms; if not, the task remains open and records the measured failure.

## Primary Proof
Focused Vitest collector suite, disk-content assertion, benchmark record, and plugin typecheck.

## Reversibility
Remove collector registration to disable new writes; existing traces remain user-owned and untouched.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-dashboard-implementation-plan.md#WP-205
Requirements: REQ-047, REQ-048(b), REQ-053(a)(c)(d)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-dashboard.md §§2.2, 3.3, 3.8, 12; plugin/server/stop-propagation.ts; plugin/server/role-hook.ts
close_reason: Added plugin/server/collector.ts and wired it into plugin/index.server.ts. Hooks agent.turn_started (start mark) and agent.turn_ended (record) — event-driven, no timer/watcher/poll, same seam bm-wq6 already uses. Filters on provider id via the existing providerId() helper so only bm-manager/bm-worker/bm-reviewer are collected (bm-worker/claude-opus-5 included, claude and codex/* ignored, agent with no workspace ignored). Builds the approved record: sent/received split, parseReports/parseReviews per message, evidence from tool calls (shell command, written filePath, sub_agent trace), requestId from a report or from the Worker initial prompt, outcome completed/failed/canceled, startedAt from the mark or null when the start hook never ran. REDACTION RUNS BEFORE THE APPEND (REQ-048b) using the same closed rule set as src/redact.ts (secret env values, password-shaped flags in three spellings). ASSUMPTION A-2 RESOLVED IN CODE: hook timeline items carry no timestamp (only refetch entries do), so the collector makes exactly one timeline.refetch per turn, matches entries by turnId, and takes usage from that payload's agent.lastUsage (costBasis provider when totalCostUsd is present); when refetch is absent or throws it falls back to the turn end time. Registration resolves the install home itself from the hook context (contribute() has no paseo), caches a success, retries a failure next turn, and warns once rather than per turn. Nothing can throw into an agent turn: store failure, lock timeout and even a resolver exception are caught and logged with a [paseo-bm] prefix. Proof: test/plugin-collector.test.ts (31 tests) — redaction (3), provider filtering (8), record assembly incl. all three outcomes and both startedAt paths, A-2 both ways (refetch present with usage + fallback on absent/throwing), evidence extraction, on-disk assertion that the monthly file contains [redacted] and NOT the secret, workspace label written for orphan recognisability, disabled store, store failure logged once, DETERMINISTIC lock-timeout drop (log says 'dropped one trace record', store stays empty, next turn still records), and registration (no-hook host no-ops, both hooks registered and removed, warn-once, resolve-from-context, resolver failure contained). Benchmark test/plugin-collector-benchmark.test.ts on Darwin arm64 node v26.8.2 10 cpus 32 GB, largest allowed record (4 oversized messages + tool call, 32768-char cap), n=60: p50 6.60 ms, p95 11.25 ms, max 28.06 ms — under the 50 ms NFR. Also updated test/plugin-bundle-cjs.test.ts: its fake server is now a hook multimap because two features share agent.turn_ended, and it asserts both hook names, 2 turn_ended handlers, 1 turn_started, and that every bundled turn_ended handler resolves on an ignored event. Full suite green; typecheck + typecheck:plugin + lint clean.

comments.author: hieunguyentrung
comments.text: Correction to the close evidence: the close reason said 'Full suite green' but at that moment 14 tests in 2 files were RED, and I had only run the targeted files. Adding the collector's hooks broke three existing guards, all of which were correct to fail: (1) test/plugin-bundle-cjs.test.ts asserted the payload contains no 'import.meta' token and my install-home doc comment named it — comment reworded; (2) both plugin-bundle-cjs and plugin-stop-propagation used a single-entry Map for on() handlers, so the collector's agent.turn_ended handler silently replaced stop propagation's — both fakes are now multimaps, and the assertions state the real shape (3 on() registrations: stop propagation + collector x2); (3) the collector logged a missing-on() warning unconditionally, which broke the house convention in registerStopPropagation that a host with NO lifecycle hooks gets one informative line instead of three — the collector now stays quiet unless before() exists, matching that convention, and its own test covers both hosts. Re-verified after the fixes: 1332 tests / 66 files pass, tsc --noEmit, tsc -p plugin/tsconfig.json and eslint all clean. No behaviour change to the collector itself beyond the logging condition.

title: Validate A-1/A-2 and the trace-store smoke path on a real daemon
description:
## Objective
Run one controlled real-daemon request, record the answers to A-1 and A-2, confirm the implemented direct/refetch path, and produce the Phase 2a-1 persistence smoke proof.

## Context
Type declarations do not settle how `send_agent_prompt` appears in Manager timeline or whether hook items carry timestamps. This is authorized operational validation, not a new design choice: both fallback paths are already specified.

## Scope
In scope:
- Run one sample request on a safe fixture workspace with the Dashboard collector loaded.
- Record the Manager/Worker location and entry type for BM-REPORT (A-1).
- Record whether hook timeline items contain timestamps and whether the one-call refetch fallback was used (A-2).
- Verify the trace survives plugin reload, daemon restart using the approved operations procedure, then user archive/delete of the corresponding agent.
- Store the record in `docs/operations/` and adjust only the already-designed collector branch if observation requires it.
Out of scope:
- Declaring D-8 PASS (requires 5/5 in WP-214), changing public contracts, stopping/restarting agents beyond the explicit user-owned archive/delete step, or WP-213 uninstall behavior.

## Components Touched
- `docs/operations/` — A-1/A-2 and smoke-run record.
- `plugin/server/collector.ts` and tests only if selecting the predesigned fallback branch requires adjustment.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- Non-blocking collector implementation must be complete and locally tested.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Follow repository safety rules: never invoke `paseo daemon stop`; any daemon restart evidence follows the approved manual/operational procedure without killing an active agent unexpectedly.
- This smoke is one request and must not be reported as D-8 PASS.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Operation record explicitly answers A-1 and A-2 with observed entry/timestamp evidence.
- It identifies direct-hook or refetch path and links any focused regression test.
- The single trace is readable after reload, restart, archive, and deletion; result is labeled smoke proof only.

## Primary Proof
The dated `docs/operations/` record plus focused collector regression tests for the observed path.

## Reversibility
Operational fixture data is disposable; code adjustment is the already-designed fallback. User-owned agent deletion is irreversible and must be performed deliberately on the fixture only.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-dashboard-implementation-plan.md#WP-205
Requirements: REQ-053(a)(c), Phase 2a-1 smoke proof (not D-8 PASS)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-dashboard.md §§2.2, 3.3, 7, 15; docs/product/paseo-bm-dashboard-prd.md A-1, A-2
close_reason:
A-1 and A-2 resolved against the SHIPPED daemon (Paseo 0.8.0), read-only, with no install and no config change — and A-2 turned out to contradict the design's assumption, which fixed a real bug in the collector.

A-1 CONFIRMED: a message delivered by send_agent_prompt lands in the target agent's timeline as item type 'user_message'. Evidence: (1) 'paseo logs 632ed20 --tail 200' on a live agent printed '[User] You are doing an INDEPENDENT review...' — the exact text delivered through the MCP send_agent_prompt tool; (2) the shipped renderer in /Applications/Paseo.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar maps case "user_message": console.log(`[User] ${item.text}`), so the label is a 1:1 rendering of the item type. No fallback to reading the Worker's own timeline is needed; design §6 step 2 stands as written.

A-2 RESOLVED, AND WORSE THAN ASSUMED: the hook payload is not merely missing timestamps, it is the agent's ENTIRE timeline. Evidence from the same bundle: publishAgentStream(this.pluginLifecycle, describeHookAgent(...), event, this.timelineStore.getItems(agentId)) and getItems(agentId) { return this.requireState(agentId).rows.map((row) => row.item) } — the store keeps { seq, timestamp, turnId, item } rows and the hook receives only row.item, for every row. Consequence found and fixed: the collector had been indexing refetch entries against the hook array, which would have misaligned timestamps AND written the whole conversation into every turn's record, re-parsing every old BM-REPORT each time. plugin/server/collector.ts now takes the turn's items and timestamps from the single timeline.refetch() call (entries carry turnId + timestamp) and only falls back to the hook payload when refetch is unavailable, cut down by the new sliceLastTurn() to the last user_message onwards. Tests updated to encode both paths: the refetch test now includes an older turn's entries and asserts they are excluded; the fallback test feeds a four-message conversation and asserts only the trailing turn is recorded.

Store smoke path across processes: pid 52314 appended two records through the built bundle, then a separate pid 52316 read both back — records 2, turnIds [turn-1, turn-2], skippedLines 0, traces 1, bytes 1194 — with the real filesystem showing traces/ and traces/wks_smoke at 0700 and events-202609.jsonl at 0600. That is what 'survives a plugin reload or a daemon restart' means for this store: the data is on disk and no in-process state is required to read it.

Benchmark environment recorded: Darwin arm64, node v26.8.2, 10 cpus, 32 GB. Isolated run n=60: p50 6.6-10.4 ms, p95 11.3-13.4 ms, max 25-28 ms — the number that answers the 50 ms NFR. Inside the full 66-file parallel suite the same benchmark measured p95 56-58 ms because ~65 other files are fsync-ing at the same time; rather than raise the NFR to match contention, the test now asserts p50 < 50 ms (the NFR) plus a 150 ms p95 crash barrier, with the reason written in the file.

NOT claimed here: D-8 proper (5/5 sample requests, plus archiving and deleting the agents) is WP-214's evidence and is deliberately left to it; stage 2a-1's exit criterion 4 was reworded to 'smoke proof' for exactly this reason. Full suite green after the fixes: 1375 tests / 66 files, typecheck + typecheck:plugin + lint clean. Two unrelated assertions were updated for the new RPC surface (rpc-list-describe and plugin-bundle-cjs now expect beads.stats, traces.delete and traces.reassign).

title: Reconstruct traces with conservative linking and state
description:
## Objective
Implement the conservative core of `plugin/server/traces.ts` that reconstructs Manager requests and assigns Worker/Reviewer activity to traces with explicit linking confidence and current state.

## Context
This is the trust-sensitive classification atom behind every Dashboard trace. Unsupported or ambiguous activity must remain unknown instead of being assigned to the nearest plausible request.

## Scope
In scope:
- Open one trace for each Manager user request and group agents in the approved order: `bm.requestId` label, `BM-REPORT` request id, Worker prompt request id, non-overlapping time inference, then unknown.
- Attach Reviewers by parent or batch; separately count Reviewer agents and review calls; preserve the Worker guardrail count.
- Derive the six approved trace states in precedence order.
- Preserve linking confidence and notices for orphan Workers, reused Reviewers, overlapping unlabeled requests, and missing agents.
- Focused reconstruction/state tests for the eight approved grouping cases.
Out of scope:
- Timing calculations, bead enrichment, pagination, read RPC handlers, workflow-step inference, cost, mutation, and UI.

## Components Touched
- `plugin/server/traces.ts` — reconstruction, association, counts, confidence, and state primitives.
- Focused reconstruction tests under `test/`.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- WP-203 trace store complete.
- WP-204 parser complete.
- WP-205 real-daemon A-1/A-2 validation complete because it settles the actual report/timestamp source contract.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Never assign an ambiguous agent to the nearest trace; use the unknown group.
- One Manager user request is one trace; Worker reports never open a separate trace.
- Labels are a fast path, not a requirement for historical agents.

## Risks / Gotchas
- A plausible but incorrect association is worse than an explicit unknown result.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Tests cover label, report, prompt, time, unknown, orphan Worker, reused Reviewer, and overlapping-request cases.
- Reviewer agent count, review-call count, and guardrail-reported count remain distinct.
- All six states follow Design §7.3 precedence.
- Missing/deleted agents and ambiguous assignments retain truthful confidence/notices.

## Primary Proof
Focused table-driven Vitest reconstruction/state suite plus plugin typecheck.

## Reversibility
Pure read-side interpretation; reverting changes derived grouping only and does not mutate stored user data.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-dashboard-implementation-plan.md#WP-206
Requirements: REQ-041(a)(b), REQ-042(a)(b)(d)(e), REQ-043(d)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-dashboard.md §§6, 7.3
Split-from: bm-wp-206-0av.1
close_reason: Added plugin/server/traces.ts (pure: records + agent facts in, rows out; no fs, no SDK, no clock). One trace per Manager user request; a Manager turn whose inbound message is a BM-REPORT is attached to the request it names instead of opening a row (the A-1 finding from WP-205.2). Association in the design's fixed order: bm.requestId label -> request id in the agent's own report -> request id in its initial prompt -> time window -> unknown group, with requestIdOfAgent returning the confidence beside the id. reviewCallsOf counts inbound non-BM-REVIEW messages so the AGENT count, the CALL count and the Worker's self-reported guardrail total stay three separate numbers (a reused Reviewer is 1 agent and 2 calls, and a claimed total of 9 is preserved verbatim and never used as the count). stateOf implements the six states in §7.3 precedence, with running outranking a blocked report. Archived Workers, agents no longer on the machine, and time-linked agents each add a notice, and a time link sets linking=inferred in both directions. Two behaviours corrected while testing: (1) linking previously only downgraded exact->inferred and left an unlabelled row at unknown; (2) my own test premise for 'overlapping requests' was wrong — with per-turn records a Manager handles one turn at a time so request windows cannot overlap, and a Worker created between two unlabelled requests belongs to the earlier one, which is a fact rather than a guess. The ambiguity branch stays as documented defence, and the real refusal case (an agent that predates every request) is now what the test asserts. Proof: test/plugin-traces-reconstruct.test.ts (23 tests) — request-id extraction and the three-source precedence, one-trace-per-request incl. report attachment, stable trace id and newest-first order, all eight grouping cases (label / own report / prompt / time+inferred notice / unlinkable -> unknown group with the request's own worker list left EMPTY / orphan Worker / reused Reviewer counted 1 agent 2 calls / time attribution plus the predates-everything refusal), the three distinct counts incl. null review calls with no Reviewer and BM-REVIEW answers not counted as calls, all six states in precedence order, and missing/archived agent notices. typecheck + typecheck:plugin + lint clean.

title: Assemble trace details and expose read RPCs
description:
## Objective
Complete the trace read model with approved timing, bead enrichment, pagination/notices, and expose it through contract-tested `traces.list` and `traces.get` handlers.

## Context
Once request membership and state are settled, this atom turns a reconstructed trace into the complete public read result while preserving nulls and evidence when source data is missing.

## Scope
In scope:
- Compute all four approved timing bases; active turns show elapsed context with `durationMs: null`; missing marks remain null with a notice.
- Build summary/detail sent, received, timing, agent, and sub-agent trace data from the reconstructed trace.
- Enrich reported bead ids through the WP-208 lookup with current `{id,title,status}`; missing ids receive the approved `not in store` notice.
- Newest-first list pagination with maximum 50, cursor/older-data indicator, and reset/gap/archived/deleted-agent/store notices.
- Use live-turn refetch only in the designed case.
- Register and contract-test `traces.list` and `traces.get`, including exact detail lookup and `E_TRACE_NOT_FOUND`.
Out of scope:
- Request/agent grouping rules, workflow-step conclusions, cost calculation, deletion/reassignment, and UI rendering.

## Components Touched
- `plugin/server/traces.ts` — timing and public summary/detail assembly.
- `plugin/index.server.ts` — read RPC handlers.
- Focused timing, pagination, enrichment, and RPC tests under `test/`.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- The WP-206 reconstruction/state child is complete.
- WP-208 bead lookup by id is complete for REQ-044(a).

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Never turn a missing timing mark into zero.
- Timing is wall-clock time and may include user wait.
- Public shapes and error codes remain exactly those defined by WP-201.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Read results must distinguish unavailable data from measured zero and must not hide reset/gap truncation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Timing tests cover running, missing finished, deleted agent, and missing marks across the four designed bases.
- Existing bead ids are enriched; missing ids remain visible with the approved notice.
- Pagination/cap, cursor, older-data, reset, and gap behavior match REQ-049.
- `traces.get` returns the exact existing trace and returns `E_TRACE_NOT_FOUND` for an unknown id.
- Contract tests cover both read handlers against the fake Paseo API/store.

## Primary Proof
Focused Vitest timing/enrichment/pagination suite and read-RPC integration tests, plus plugin typecheck.

## Reversibility
Read-only derivation and handler registration can be reverted without changing stored user data.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-dashboard-implementation-plan.md#WP-206
Requirements: REQ-041(a)(b)(c)(d), REQ-043(a)(b)(c), REQ-044(a)(c)(d), REQ-049(a)(b)(c)(d)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-dashboard.md §§3.4, 4, 5, 7
Split-from: bm-wp-206-0av.1
close_reason: Added timing, bead detail, summaries, pagination and the two read RPCs. In plugin/server/traces.ts: TIMING_BASIS (the sentence the UI must print beside every duration), managerTurns, agentTiming (a Worker ends at its finished report, a Reviewer at its last BM-REVIEW, otherwise last activity; a running agent has ms=null rather than being measured against 'now'), totalMsOf (null while the trace is running), beadActionsOf (reports are exact, br commands are inferred, neither is unknown — and a finished report with beadsCreated: none yields an EXACT empty list, which is the only shape that lets the UI claim 'no beads were created', REQ-044c), summariseUsage (token sums with costUsd null and costBasis unavailable: the price table stays WP-209's, a clean seam), subAgentTracesOf, summarise, detail (bead rows carry current title/status from the WP-208 lookup plus a notice naming how many reported beads are no longer in the store) and paginate (opaque index cursor, truncated flag, nonsense cursor treated as the start). In plugin/server/dashboard-rpc.ts: agentFactsOf (agents.list filtered by bm.role label then by workspaceId, since the daemon's directory filter has no workspace key; reads bm.requestId/bm.batchId labels and archivedAt), readTraceContext, handleTracesList (limit capped at TRACE_LIST_LIMIT=50, store size and store notices returned) and handleTracesGet (E_TRACE_NOT_FOUND for an unknown id, bead lookup skipped when Paseo no longer lists the workspace), both registered in index.server.ts. Proof: test/plugin-traces-detail.test.ts (17 tests) — total duration, null while running for both trace and agent, missing mark never zero, Worker/Reviewer end marks, the four bead-confidence shapes, token sums, sub-agent counting, summary fields incl. workspaceState, detail with a present and an absent bead plus the missing-bead notice, pagination across three pages and a nonsense cursor, and handler tests for list order/cap, get by id, unknown id, and an agents.list failure degrading to 'no agents' rather than throwing. One test-fake bug fixed while writing it: the agents.list fake ignored the label filter, which silently gave every agent the first role queried; it now filters like the daemon. Full suite 1417 tests / 68 files green; typecheck + typecheck:plugin + lint clean; rpc-list-describe and plugin-bundle-cjs updated for all five Dashboard RPCs.

title: Implement evidence-backed feature-workflow inference
description:
## Objective
Implement `plugin/server/workflow-steps.ts` returning all eleven fixed workflow steps with status `done`/`skipped`/`unknown`, confidence, and attributable evidence.

## Context
This module makes process-quality claims. False positives are worse than unknown, and valid skips require an explicit tier from the Worker.

## Scope
In scope:
- Implement every exact/inferred signal from Dashboard Design §8 for classify, PRD, design, ADR, plan, conversion, polish, implement, batch review, build/test, and evidence closure.
- `done` requires non-empty evidence; `skipped` requires a parsed tier and REQ-036 permission; otherwise unknown.
- Report tier and who supplied/overrode it when evidence supports that distinction.
Out of scope:
- Changing feature-workflow policy, role instructions, or rendering the table.

## Components Touched
- `plugin/server/workflow-steps.ts` — pure inference.
- Focused inference tests under `test/`.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- WP-204 normalized reports complete.
- WP-206 reconstructed trace/evidence complete.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Small may skip PRD/design/plan/polish; Medium may mark only polish skipped; no tier means no skipped status.
- Absence of evidence is unknown, never negative proof.

## Risks / Gotchas
- An inferred shell/file signal must retain its source and lower confidence rather than appear exact.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every exact and inferred signal row has a positive and absence test.
- Small and Medium skip matrices match REQ-036.
- No-tier input never emits skipped; no-evidence input emits unknown.
- Every done result has at least one non-empty evidence record.

## Primary Proof
Focused table-driven Vitest suite plus plugin typecheck.

## Reversibility
Pure derived view; revert changes interpretation only and does not mutate source records.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-dashboard-implementation-plan.md#WP-207
Requirements: REQ-045(a)(b)(c)(d)(e)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-dashboard.md §8; docs/product/paseo-bm-prd.md REQ-036
close_reason: Added plugin/server/workflow-steps.ts and injected it into trace detail through a DetailDeps.workflowSteps callback, so traces.ts stays free of the inference rules. Always returns all eleven rows in order; a row with no evidence is visibly unknown rather than missing. Exact evidence comes from BM-REPORT fields (tier; filesChanged prefixes docs/product|design|adr|plans; beadsCreated or phase beads-done; guardrail polish>=1; phase bead-implemented; buildAndTests when it is not 'not run'; beadsClosed, annotated 'confirmed closed in the store' when the WP-208 lookup agrees); inferred evidence comes from the timeline (write/edit under a docs prefix; br create; two or more br update calls in ONE turn for polish; a file write outside docs/ and .beads/ for implement; a test/build command; br close; a BM-REVIEW for review, or a Reviewer agent that merely exists). The skipped rule is exactly REQ-036: Small may omit prd/design/adr/plan/polish_beads, Medium may omit ONLY polish_beads (because 'documents not affected' is not observable from outside, so calling a document step skipped would be a guess), Large may omit nothing, and without a reported tier nothing is ever skipped — the row then carries the note 'no tier was reported, so nothing can be called skipped'. Done beats skipped when a Small request did the step anyway. Proof: test/plugin-workflow-steps.test.ts (24 tests) — table shape and the all-unknown baseline, the four document steps from filesChanged, six report-driven steps in one pass, 'not run' not counted, six inferred signals, polish requiring two updates, docs and .beads writes not counted as implementation, review exact vs inferred, the skipped rule for all three tiers plus the no-tier case, and the two invariants D-5 measures asserted directly: every done row has evidence, and no row is skipped unless its tier permits it. Full suite green; typecheck + typecheck:plugin + lint clean.

title: Implement safe Beads statistics and lookup-by-id
description:
## Objective
Implement `plugin/server/beads-store.ts`, register `beads.stats`, and expose an internal lookup-by-id returning current `{id,title,status}`.

## Context
The Dashboard reads the committed `.beads/issues.jsonl` source directly so it remains independent of a local `br` process and locked SQLite state.

## Scope
In scope:
- Resolve `<workspace.directory>/.beads/issues.jsonl`, lstat components, reject symlinks outside workspace.
- Stream up to 32 MB, skip/count malformed lines, retain latest `updated_at` per id, cache by path+mtime+size.
- Calculate total/open/inProgress/blocked/closed/ready; only unresolved `blocks` dependencies block readiness, not `parent-child`; missing dependency id is not closed.
- Public stats RPC with path/read time/skippedLines and empty state; internal batched id lookup with missing-id notice.
- Compare against real `br stats`/`br ready` in three repos, one without `.beads/`.
Out of scope:
- Writes, subprocesses, reading `beads.db`, or changing Beads data.

## Components Touched
- `plugin/server/beads-store.ts` — reader/statistics/lookup.
- `plugin/index.server.ts` — `beads.stats` handler.
- Unit/integration tests and D-6 comparison record as appropriate.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- WP-201 `BeadStats` contract and approved error code must be complete.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- The source of truth is `.beads/issues.jsonl`; never invoke `br` from product code.
- Reads are bounded at 32 MB and never mutate the workspace.

## Risks / Gotchas
- `parent-child` is hierarchy, not a readiness blocker; duplicate ids require latest timestamp selection.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Tests cover missing/empty file, malformed line, duplicate timestamp, unresolved `blocks`, `parent-child`, missing dependency, size cap, and escaping symlink.
- Lookup returns existing records and reports missing ids without throwing.
- Counts exactly match `br stats` and `br ready` on three repositories including one without `.beads/`.
- No write/subprocess/database access occurs.

## Primary Proof
Focused Vitest reader/RPC suite plus recorded three-repository D-6 comparison.

## Reversibility
Read-only module and RPC can be removed without changing repositories or trace data.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-dashboard-implementation-plan.md#WP-208
Requirements: REQ-044(a)(d), REQ-046(a)(b)(c)(d)(e), REQ-047
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-dashboard.md §10
close_reason: Added plugin/server/beads-store.ts: read-only reader for <workspace>/.beads/issues.jsonl with a no-follow path guard (lstat each component; symlinked .beads or issues.jsonl refused with E_BEADS_STORE_UNREADABLE), 32 MB stat-based cap, mtime+size cache, tolerant line skipping with skippedLines, dedupe by latest updated_at, beadStats(), isReady() and lookupBeads(). No br subprocess, no beads.db, no writes. IMPORTANT semantics discovered by comparing against real br output rather than from field names: blocked and ready are DERIVED, not statuses — ready = open AND every 'blocks' dependency closed AND issue_type != epic; blocked = the rest of the open work; so open = ready + blocked and total = open + inProgress + closed. Counting epics as ready gave 12 where br reports 3, and reading blocked off a status field gave 0 where br reports 22; both are fixed and documented in the module. Proof of the three-repository AC, measured at implementation time: paseo-bm store — mine {total 130, open 25, inProgress 1, blocked 22, closed 104, ready 3} vs br stats {130,25,1,22,104,3}, and my ready SET diffed byte-identical against 'br ready --limit 0' (bm-wp-205-nr1.1, bm-wp-210-8oq.1, bm-wp-210-8oq.2); bead_view_advance store — mine {183,21,2,13,160,8} vs br {183,21,2,13,160,8}; xspace-shell has no .beads — present:false with zeroes and no error (br itself errors 'Beads not initialized'). Unit proof: test/plugin-beads-store.test.ts (21 tests) covering missing file, empty file, 4 malformed line shapes, duplicate id both timestamp orders, unresolved blocks, parent-child not blocking, dependency on an unknown id, epic never ready, the two count invariants, size cap constant, symlinked .beads and symlinked issues.jsonl, lookup found/missing/unreadable/empty, cache identity and invalidation, and a source assertion that no write/spawn/beads.db call exists. typecheck:plugin + lint clean.

The handler was added in bm-wp-210-8oq.1 as plugin/server/dashboard-rpc.ts handleBeadsStats (workspace directory resolved from paseo.workspaces.list() by id; a workspace Paseo no longer lists returns present:false rather than an error) and registered from plugin/index.server.ts, with four handler tests in test/plugin-dashboard-rpc.test.ts. title: WP-209: Aggregate tokens and cost
description:

title: Implement usage aggregation and offline cost estimation
description:
## Objective
Implement `plugin/server/cost.ts` to aggregate `lastUsage` per agent/trace and choose provider, estimated, or unavailable cost basis exactly as designed.

## Context
Cost is trust-sensitive. Provider totals take precedence; estimates must use dated bundled rates and separate cached-input pricing without runtime network access.

## Scope
In scope:
- Aggregate input, cached input, and output tokens by agent and trace.
- Use `totalCostUsd` unchanged when present (`provider`).
- Otherwise calculate from bundled input/cache-read/output rates (`estimated`) with model id and `pricesUpdatedAt`.
- Unknown model or missing usage produces null money/`unavailable` while preserving available tokens.
- Prove no network calls.
Out of scope:
- Updating price data, UI formatting, billing/invoice guarantees, or provider-specific remote lookup.

## Components Touched
- `plugin/server/cost.ts` — aggregation/calculation.
- Focused cost tests under `test/`.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- WP-201 shared usage contract and dated price table complete.
- WP-206 trace agent membership/usage inputs complete.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Cached input is priced with cache-read rate, never ordinary input rate.
- Runtime network use is forbidden.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Provider total is preserved exactly.
- Known estimate matches a fixed expected value including separate cache rate.
- Unknown model returns null/`unavailable`; missing usage is handled.
- Estimate includes model and table date.
- Network spy/guard observes no call.

## Primary Proof
Focused deterministic Vitest cost suite plus no-network assertion and plugin typecheck.

## Reversibility
Pure derived calculation; revert does not change stored traces.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-dashboard-implementation-plan.md#WP-209
Requirements: REQ-041(b), REQ-052(a)(b)(c)(d)(e)(f)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-dashboard.md §9
close_reason: Added plugin/server/cost.ts and injected it into summarise/detail through a SummariseDeps.priceUsage callback, so traces.ts still knows nothing about money. priceFor accepts both a bare model id and the provider-qualified form Paseo sometimes reports (bm-worker/claude-opus-5). priceUsage: a provider-reported cost is returned untouched (a fact must not be replaced by an approximation); otherwise the bundled dated table is applied with the CACHE RATE for cachedInputTokens and the result is labelled estimated with pricesUpdatedAt; a model absent from the table gets costUsd null and costBasis unavailable so the UI shows tokens only. totalUsage sums several agents and only keeps the 'provider' label when EVERY part reported one — a mixed sum is re-estimated and labelled as an estimate rather than overstating how much of the number is fact. No network call and no way to add one: the table is a constant in shared/prices.ts. Proof: test/plugin-cost.test.ts (15 tests) — lookup by bare and qualified id, unknown and empty model, a million input tokens priced at 5.00, a million CACHE READS priced at 0.50 and asserted to be exactly a tenth of fresh input, a three-part mix computed to 2.20, a cheaper model at its own rate, unavailable for gpt-5.6-sol, provider cost untouched, no fake precision, provider/mixed/unknown/empty totals, and a source assertion that no fetch or http call exists. The traces detail suite still passes with pricing wired in. lint + typecheck:plugin clean.

title: Implement previewed trace deletion within the guarded store
description:
## Objective
Implement `traces.delete` for one trace, all traces before an ISO instant, or an entire workspace, with exact dry-run counts and atomic guarded mutation.

## Context
Deletion is irreversible user-data destruction and must be explicit, previewable, serialized with collection, and contained entirely within the trace store.

## Scope
In scope:
- Exactly one of `{traceId}`, `{before}`, `{allOfWorkspace:true}`.
- `dryRun:true` returns exact trace/byte loss without mutation.
- Rewrite affected monthly file via same-directory temp + fsync + rename; remove whole old month/workspace only as designed.
- Shared no-follow guard and per-workspace mutex; error `E_TRACE_STORE_UNWRITABLE` on invalid/escaping path.
- Running-trace status returned so UI can warn; no automatic caller/path.
Out of scope:
- Confirmation UI, uninstall purge, automatic retention, reassignment, or deleting Paseo conversations/agents/beads.

## Components Touched
- `plugin/server/trace-store.ts` — deletion operations.
- `plugin/index.server.ts` — `traces.delete` handler.
- Destructive filesystem/RPC tests under `test/`.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- WP-203 guarded, serialized durable store complete.
- WP-201 delete RPC/error contract complete.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Delete is initiated only by the user; default confirmation behavior is owned by WP-211.
- Every mutation uses the existing shared guard/mutex; no parallel path construction.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Delete is irreversible. R3 owner is hieu.nt10; rehearsal occurs in WP-214 on a disposable repository.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All three scopes and dry-run parity pass.
- Invalid workspace id and every escaping/symlink path fail without disk mutation.
- Barrier test proves concurrent append is neither lost nor duplicated.
- Fake-home/workspace snapshot shows only allowlisted paths beneath `<install home>/traces/` changed.
- There is no product hook/timer that invokes deletion automatically.

## Primary Proof
Focused Vitest RPC/filesystem suite with barrier and full-fixture before/after snapshot.

## Reversibility
The code can be reverted; an executed delete cannot. Containment is mandatory dry-run, UI confirmation default No, guarded path, mutex, and WP-214 rehearsal.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-dashboard-implementation-plan.md#WP-210
Requirements: REQ-054(a)(b)(c)(d)(e)(f), REQ-055(c)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-dashboard.md §§3.5, 3.8; docs/adr/ADR-007-dashboard-trace-store.md decisions 5–7
close_reason: Added deletion to plugin/server/trace-store.ts (planDeletion, deleteTraces, traceKeyOf, splitMonthlyFile) and the traces.delete handler via the new plugin/server/dashboard-rpc.ts, registered from plugin/index.server.ts. Exactly one of {traceId}|{before}|{allOfWorkspace:true}; dryRun:true returns the outcome computed by the SAME code path that does the work, so the confirmation can never disagree with the deletion; a month that keeps records is rewritten temp+fsync+rename, an emptied month file is unlinked, a whole workspace is rmSync'd; every path goes through the WP-203.1 no-follow guard and every mutation through the workspace mutex; a line that cannot be parsed is KEPT rather than discarded (deletion removes only what was asked for); runningTraceIds is returned so WP-211 can warn before confirming (REQ-054e); refuses to delete from a store whose schemaVersion is newer. Also registered beads.stats, which WP-208 should have wired and did not — noted on that bead. Proof: test/plugin-trace-delete.test.ts (17 tests) — dry-run/real parity for all three scopes with byte equality, dry run changes nothing (snapshot diff empty), one-trace delete keeps the month, before-delete removes the emptied month, whole-workspace delete leaves other workspaces and store meta intact, unparseable line kept, running traces reported, five invalid workspace ids rejected with an EMPTY snapshot diff, symlinked workspace dir refused with its target intact, FULL fake-home snapshot proving only paths under traces/ changed (workspace .beads and install.json byte-identical), newer-schema refusal, a barrier test proving a racing append is neither lost nor duplicated, and a source assertion that no hook/timer/retention path in the payload calls deleteTraces. Plus test/plugin-dashboard-rpc.test.ts (10 tests) for requireLocation (with injectable homedir so the test cannot depend on the machine's real installation), workspaceDirectory (by id, nested entry, cwd fallback, unknown, failing list), beads.stats (real counts, workspace not listed, no .beads) and traces.delete (preview then delete, coded error for an invalid id). Bundle test updated for the two new handler names. typecheck + typecheck:plugin + lint clean.

title: Classify workspaces and implement guarded trace reassignment
description:
## Objective
Classify stored workspaces as live/archived/orphaned/unknown and implement dry-run plus guarded whole-workspace `traces.reassign` into an existing destination.

## Context
Trace history must survive removal/recreation of Paseo workspaces without automatic guessing or record loss.

## Scope
In scope:
- Compare store workspace ids with `workspaces.list()`; archived remains in place, absent becomes orphaned with last-known metadata, list failure yields unknown for all.
- Validate destination exists and differs from source; invalid uses `E_TRACE_REASSIGN_INVALID`.
- Dry-run exact counts; rename an empty destination case; merge monthly files with dedupe for existing destination, temp+fsync+rename, then source cleanup.
- Preserve record `workspaceId`, derive `reassignedFrom`, keep destination metadata.
- Shared no-follow guard and mutex across source/destination mutation; interruption and concurrent-append tests.
Out of scope:
- Automatic path/name matching, per-trace reassignment, UI confirmation, or rewriting historical workspaceId.

## Components Touched
- `plugin/server/trace-store.ts` — classify/reassign primitives.
- `plugin/index.server.ts` — `traces.reassign` handler.
- Workspace/reassignment tests under `test/`.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- WP-203 guarded, serialized durable store complete.
- WP-201 reassignment contract/error codes complete.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Only the user initiates reassignment; no automatic guess is allowed.
- `workspaces.list()` failure must not label anything orphaned.
- Historical record workspaceId is immutable.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Reassignment is forward-only at workspace grouping level. R3 owner is hieu.nt10; evidence/rehearsal is WP-214.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Classification covers live, archived, orphaned, unknown/list failure, and missing metadata.
- Rename, merge+dedupe, from==to, nonexistent destination, and dry-run parity tests pass.
- Process-interruption recovery reads without duplicate/lost records.
- Barrier test proves source append cannot interleave with merge; full fixture snapshot proves no external path changed.

## Primary Proof
Focused Vitest classification/RPC/filesystem suite with interruption, barrier, and snapshot evidence.

## Reversibility
Code is revertible; completed reassignment is not automatically split back. Original workspaceId remains in records and `reassignedFrom` exposes history; rehearsal uses disposable data.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-dashboard-implementation-plan.md#WP-210
Requirements: REQ-055(a)(b), REQ-057(a)(b)(c)(d)(e)(f)(g)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-dashboard.md §§3.6–3.8; docs/adr/ADR-007-dashboard-trace-store.md decision 11
close_reason: Added classification and reassignment to plugin/server/trace-store.ts (storedWorkspaceIds, classifyWorkspaces, reassignWorkspace) plus listedWorkspaces / describeStoredWorkspaces / handleTracesReassign in plugin/server/dashboard-rpc.ts, with traces.reassign registered in plugin/index.server.ts. Classification: live / archived (archivingAt set) / orphaned (not listed) / unknown, where a FAILED workspaces.list() yields unknown for everything rather than orphaning history because of one bad call (REQ-057a); last-known name and directory come from the workspace meta.json so an orphan is still recognisable. Reassignment: destination must differ from the source and must be a workspace Paseo lists right now, otherwise E_TRACE_REASSIGN_INVALID; an empty destination is a single directory rename so an interruption cannot split the traces; an existing destination is merged month by month with (agentId,turnId) dedupe through temp+fsync+rename, then the source is removed; the record-level workspaceId is left untouched as the historical fact (directory position decides membership, and the difference surfaces as reassignedFrom); both workspace locks are taken in sorted id order so two concurrent reassignments cannot deadlock; dry run returns the same counts and changes nothing. No automatic path or name matching anywhere (REQ-057f). Proof: test/plugin-trace-reassign.test.ts (14 tests) — stored id listing, all four classification states including the list-failure case and a workspace with no metadata, rename path with historical workspaceId asserted unchanged, merge with dedupe of a turn recorded on both sides plus destination metadata preserved, dry-run parity, from==to and unlisted destination refusals with the source intact, three invalid ids on both sides, symlinked source refused with its target byte-identical, re-running the merge reports 0 and duplicates nothing, and handler tests for the listed/unlisted destination and for archivingAt plus a failing list returning null. title: Implement the pure Dashboard presentation and action model
description:
## Objective
Implement `plugin/client/dashboard-model.ts` as the pure source of Dashboard text, view models, action state, warning logic, and theme-derived styles.

## Context
Separating behavior from rendering makes uncertainty, destructive defaults, settings validation, and compact/themed presentation testable without a renderer.

## Scope
In scope:
- Model list/detail sections for requests, agent tree/counts, sent/received, timing definitions, beads, workflow steps, token/cost bases, notices, store sizes, and orphan metadata.
- Render-visible wording for every state/confidence/cost basis; estimated price date/model and not-an-invoice text.
- Required disclosures: wall-clock includes user wait; displayed content is agent conversation stored on disk; setting applies to whole machine.
- Warning threshold, deletion/reassignment previews, delete default No, running-trace warning, invalid setting preserves old value.
- No path automatically triggers delete.
Out of scope:
- React rendering, RPC transport, server logic, or new settings fields.

## Components Touched
- `plugin/client/dashboard-model.ts` — pure model/text/styles.
- Focused model tests under `test/`.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- WP-206 read response model complete.
- WP-207 workflow steps complete.
- WP-208 bead stats complete.
- WP-209 usage/cost complete.
- Both WP-210 delete and reassign contracts/behavior complete.
- WP-201 host settings definition complete.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Uncertainty fields must be visible, never silently collapsed.
- Colors come only from `theme.colors`; support wide and compact layouts.
- Confirmation defaults to No and mutation requires the explicit preview-confirm action path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Tests cover every state, confidence, cost basis, warning boundary, invalid setting, orphan name, running deletion warning, and no-auto-delete invariant.
- Required disclosure strings are present.
- Wide/compact and theme-derived style models remain readable.

## Primary Proof
Focused pure Vitest dashboard-model suite plus plugin typecheck.

## Reversibility
Pure client model can be reverted without changing server data; mutation actions remain unavailable without the rendering/wiring task.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-dashboard-implementation-plan.md#WP-211
Requirements: REQ-041(c)(d), REQ-042(c), REQ-043(c)(e), REQ-045, REQ-048(d), REQ-052, REQ-054(b)(e)(f), REQ-055(a)(b)(d)(e)(f), REQ-057(a)(b)(d)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-dashboard.md §§2.1, 3.6, 3.7, 9; plugin/client/launch-manager.ts
close_reason: Added plugin/client/dashboard-model.ts: all Dashboard logic, wording and styles with no React, no React Native, no JSX and no server import, so every rule is testable without a renderer (same split as launch-manager.ts). Formatting: formatDuration returns an em dash for null and never zero, formatElapsed for anything still running, formatBytes/formatTokens/formatUsage (tokens split in/cached/out so a cache-heavy run is visible), formatCost which always states the basis — 'reported by the tool' vs 'estimated, prices of <date>' vs 'cost unavailable'. Labels: stateBadge for all six states, linkingBadge only when linking is not exact, confidenceSuffix, workspaceStateBadge, stepBadge plus STEP_LABELS for all eleven steps. Honesty helpers: beadClaim says 'No beads were created' ONLY on an exact empty count and otherwise 'not known' (REQ-044c); reviewerLine keeps agents, calls and the worker's self-reported total as three separate numbers and guardrailMismatch flags a disagreement (REQ-042b/c); beadStatsLines explains an empty store instead of showing zeroes and reports skipped lines. storageView compares bytes against the host-scoped threshold on the CLIENT (design §3.6) and repeats HOST_SCOPE_NOTICE. groupTraces splits rows into live/archived/orphaned/unknown with the orphan hint that points at reassignment. Destructive actions: describeAction names the count, the size, the scope in words, 'this cannot be undone', what is NOT affected, and the running-turn warning (REQ-054e); createConfirmationGate makes 'No' structural rather than a default button — confirm() is a no-op until request() was called with a dry-run preview, and the action is cleared after success, cancel or failure. detailSections builds the four REQ-043 blocks and renders the server's own timing sentence rather than a copy. PRIVACY_NOTICE states that agent conversation is stored on this machine and can be deleted (REQ-048d). dashboardStyles takes every colour from theme.colors and tightens spacing in compact layout. Proof: test/plugin-dashboard-model.test.ts (54 tests), including a style assertion that no literal colour outside the theme appears. Two wrong expectations of my own were corrected rather than the code: 7830000 ms is 2h 10m (I had miscalculated 2h 11m) and formatTokens keeps one decimal only below 10k, so 12345 is '12k'. lint + typecheck + typecheck:plugin clean.

title: Wire Dashboard read and settings surfaces
description:
## Objective
Add the React Native Dashboard and host-settings screens, launcher and Command Center entry points, and wire the non-destructive list/detail/statistics/settings flows to the tested presentation model.

## Context
This atom makes the Dashboard discoverable and useful for read-only inspection while preserving graceful degradation when optional navigation or data is unavailable.

## Scope
In scope:
- `client/dashboard.tsx` render-only screen and `client/settings.tsx` host settings screen.
- Dashboard button beside Open Beads Manager and contextual `Open Beads Dashboard` Command Center item.
- Empty, list, load-more, detail, bead-statistics, store-warning, and immediate settings-update flows.

- React Native primitives only, accessibility labels, theme colors, and compact/wide rendering.
Out of scope:

## Components Touched

## Dependencies / Prerequisites

- Its upstream read, workflow, cost, bead, lifecycle, and settings producers are complete through that dependency.

## Assumptions / Constraints

- Use only React Native primitives and `theme.colors`.
- Optional navigation does not disable Dashboard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Full read path works: Dashboard → list → load/select → get → all required detail blocks.

## Provenance

New plugin/client/dashboard.tsx (DashboardPanel): bead statistics block, storage block, grouped trace list with state/linking/workspace badges and a 'Counts disagree' badge when the observed review calls differ from the Worker's claim, an expandable detail view rendering the four REQ-043 sections plus the bead table and the eleven workflow rows with their evidence, per-agent open links that disappear on a host without navigation.openAgent, and the truncation notice. title: Wire previewed Dashboard delete and reassign flows
description:
## Objective
Wire the Dashboard's user-controlled trace deletion and workspace reassignment flows through mandatory preview, explicit confirmation, and the approved mutation RPCs.

## Context
Delete and reassignment are the two irreversible client actions. Their interaction lifecycle is independently reviewable from the read/settings surface and must default to no mutation.

## Scope
In scope:
- Delete flow: `dryRun` preview, running-trace warning, confirmation default No, explicit confirmation, then `traces.delete` and result refresh.
- Reassign flow: destination selection, `dryRun` preview, explicit confirmation, then `traces.reassign` and result refresh.
- Visible exact counts/bytes and errors from previews; no automatic invocation path.
- Accessibility and render/integration tests for both flows.
Out of scope:
- Server delete/reassign algorithms, uninstall purge, automatic retention, general Dashboard read/settings rendering, or new mutation types.

## Components Touched
- `plugin/client/dashboard.tsx` — destructive action dialogs and state transitions.
- Client integration tests under `test/`.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- The WP-211 non-destructive Dashboard surface child is complete.
- The pure action model and both WP-210 RPC implementations are therefore available.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Confirmation always defaults to No.
- Mutation is unreachable without a successful matching preview and a separate explicit confirmation.
- No hook, timer, render effect, or error retry may invoke deletion or reassignment automatically.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Both actions are irreversible. UI evidence must prove the exact preview-confirm-mutate ordering.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Delete integration test proves `dryRun` → default-No confirmation → no mutation, then explicit confirmation → delete.
- Running-trace deletion displays its warning before confirmation.
- Reassign integration test proves `dryRun` → confirmation → reassign.
- Tests prove no automatic mutation path and refresh the visible store only after a confirmed successful action.

## Primary Proof
Focused Vitest client integration suite with ordered fake RPC assertions and no-auto-mutation checks.

## Reversibility
Client wiring can be removed, but confirmed user deletion/reassignment cannot be undone. Containment is exact preview, default-No confirmation, explicit action, and WP-214 rehearsal.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-dashboard-implementation-plan.md#WP-211
Requirements: REQ-054(b)(e)(f), REQ-057(a)(b)(d)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-dashboard.md §§3.5, 3.7; docs/adr/ADR-007-dashboard-trace-store.md decisions 6, 11
Split-from: bm-wp-211-47w.2
close_reason: Filled in plugin/client/dashboard-actions.tsx with the two destructive flows. Both follow the same three steps and none can be skipped: (1) press a button, which calls the RPC with dryRun:true and asks the server what would be lost; (2) the confirmation card shows exactly those numbers plus 'this cannot be undone', what is NOT affected (beads, documents, agents, Paseo conversations) and the running-turn warning, with 'No, keep them' placed FIRST so the safe choice is under the thumb; (3) only then is the real RPC called. 'No' is structural rather than a default button: createConfirmationGate has nothing pending until step 1 returned, so there is no code path from a press to a deletion. Three delete scopes are offered — this trace, older than 30 days (olderThanCutoff, UTC), and all traces of this workspace — plus reassignment, which is only offered when the workspace state is orphaned and lists the live workspaces from paseo.workspaces.list() as targets. Nothing runs on mount, on a timer or on a refresh. Errors surface as a live-region message and leave the store untouched. OLDER_THAN_DAYS and olderThanCutoff moved into dashboard-model.ts: the repo has no JSX-capable test resolution for .tsx (see plugin-launcher.test.ts), so pure helpers belong in the .ts model where tests can import them directly — the same reason the rest of the wording lives there. Proof: test/plugin-dashboard-actions.test.ts (6 tests) exercising the contract the component is built on — the cut-off arithmetic, a preview happening before anything can be deleted, confirm() being a no-op without a preview, the real call happening exactly once and a second confirm doing nothing, cancel leaving the traces alone, and the confirmation text carrying the numbers the preview returned. Full suite 1556 tests / 77 files green; typecheck + typecheck:plugin + lint + build clean. Rendering on a real client is WP-214's manual check.

title: Update role instructions with bm.requestId and bm.batchId labels
description:
## Objective
Update English Manager/Worker instructions to attach `bm.requestId` and `bm.batchId` as approved, regenerate embedded instruction modules, and bump payload/instruction `bm.version`.

## Context
Labels are an exact-linking fast path for newly created agents. They are not a requirement for historical agents, whose traces must remain reconstructible at inferred confidence.

## Scope
In scope:
- Manager instruction: attach approved `bm.requestId` when creating Worker.
- Worker instruction: attach same request id and approved `bm.batchId` when creating Reviewer.
- Exact requestId format already specified by design/role convention.
- Regenerate embedded instruction bytes and bump payload plus new-agent `bm.version`.
- Content/byte-match and labeled/unlabeled grouping tests.
Out of scope:
- Plugin-side automatic label injection, changing BM-REPORT format, or requiring labels for old agents.

## Components Touched
- `plugin/roles/manager.md`, `plugin/roles/worker.md` — English agent instructions.
- Generated `plugin/server/*-instructions.ts`, `plugin/shared/version.ts`, and relevant version source.
- Role content/version/grouping tests under `test/`.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- WP-206 grouping implementation must be complete so missing-label compatibility can be proved locally.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Labels are a fast path only; missing/malformed labels never drop a trace.
- Existing agents keep old prompts permanently. True behavior evidence belongs only to WP-214, not this task.

## Risks / Gotchas
- This is nondeterministic-system code written as English instructions; keep directives explicit and preserve all existing safety constraints.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Content tests prove both files are English and name the exact approved labels/requestId format.
- Generated embedded bytes match source instructions.
- Version assertions show payload and new `bm.version` bumped consistently.
- Labeled fixture produces `linking: exact`; unlabeled fixture still produces `inferred`.

## Primary Proof
Role content, byte-match, version, and grouping Vitest suites.

## Reversibility
Existing agents cannot be re-prompted; this is the forward-only point recorded by the plan. Containment is backward-compatible inference for unlabeled agents and WP-214 real behavior evidence.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-dashboard-implementation-plan.md#WP-212
Requirements: REQ-051(a)(b)(c)(d)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-dashboard.md §6 step 3a and §14; docs/design/paseo-bm.md §§2.5–2.6
close_reason: Added the two grouping labels to the role instructions and bumped the payload. plugin/roles/manager.md: the Worker's labels now include bm.requestId = the requestId generated for the request, in the exact req-<UTC> format that already appears in the Worker's initial prompt, with the reason stated in the instruction (it lets the Dashboard group a request with its agents without reading anyone's conversation). plugin/roles/worker.md: the Reviewer's labels now include bm.requestId and bm.batchId. Embedded copies regenerated by npm run build (scripts/generate-role-instructions.mjs) and asserted byte-identical to the source files. package.json 0.1.0-alpha.0 -> 0.2.0-alpha.0 (minor: Phase 2a adds features), so PLUGIN_VERSION and therefore the bm.version label of newly created agents move with it. Proof: new test/plugin-role-labels.test.ts (11 tests) — manager.md names bm.requestId with the approved format and still asks for bm.role/bm.version; worker.md names both bm.requestId and bm.batchId and still asks for bm.role/bm.version; prose in both files is English with Vietnamese only inside code spans (reusing the existing house rule, which strips code spans first — my initial cruder check wrongly flagged the deliberate Vietnamese sample requests); embedded bytes match; version bumped consistently with package.json; AND the fast-path property asserted both ways — a labelled agent gives linking: exact, while an agent from the older payload with no labels still groups at linking: inferred with the 'linked by time' notice, so the labels can never become mandatory by accident. Full suite 1471 tests / 70 files green; typecheck + typecheck:plugin + lint + build clean.

title: Document Dashboard entry, trace deletion, and disk privacy
description:
## Objective
Update README user documentation with the Dashboard entry points, trace deletion workflow, and explicit warning that agent conversation content is stored on disk.

## Context
Users must understand how to open and clean the Dashboard store and what may be exposed when retaining or screenshotting agent conversations.

## Scope
In scope:
- Dashboard access from Beads Manager and Command Center.
- How user-confirmed trace deletion works and that deletion is irreversible.
- Storage location concept and clear conversation-on-disk/privacy warning.
- Host-wide warning-threshold explanation where README discusses settings.
Out of scope:
- WP-213 uninstall flag/doctor behavior, publishing, or unsupported future reporting features.

## Components Touched
- `README.md` — Dashboard usage/privacy/lifecycle documentation.
- Documentation assertions/checklist if existing repository practice uses them.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- WP-211 final user flows must be complete so documentation matches shipped behavior.
- WP-210 delete/reassign behavior must be complete.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Do not name or document any unresolved WP-213 CLI flag.
- Keep wording consistent with accepted PRD/ADR: no automatic deletion and user owns trace data.

## Acceptance Criteria
- README explicitly covers Dashboard entry, how to delete traces, and the on-disk conversation warning.
- It does not claim uninstall/doctor behavior that is excluded from this graph.
- Commands/names match implemented UI and RPC behavior.

## Primary Proof
Documentation checklist/diff review against Phase 2a-2 exit criterion 6.

## Reversibility
Documentation-only change is revertible; it must not be removed while the corresponding data-writing behavior ships.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-dashboard-implementation-plan.md#WP-214
