title: Run real-daemon Dashboard acceptance for D-1 through D-11
description:
## Objective
Create the Dashboard acceptance checklist and run record, then measure D-1 through D-11 on a real Paseo daemon using the approved five-request fixture and disposable repository data.

## Context
This is the only evidence owner for live agent grouping/workflow accuracy, persistence across lifecycle events, and harmless destructive operations. CI does not run real agents.

## Scope
In scope:
- `docs/operations/` checklist with fixture, exact metric methods, and record template.
- Run five approved sample requests; measure D-1, D-2–D-5 on all five, D-6 on three repos including one without `.beads/`, and D-7 throughout.
- D-8 after reload, approved daemon restart procedure, archive, and delete for 5/5 samples.
- D-9 one-trace and whole-workspace deletion with machine-filesystem before/after evidence; D-10 provider/estimate comparison; D-11 reassign with loss/duplication and filesystem evidence.
- One real version update proving the store remains byte-preserved.
- Honest PASS/No values and measurements.
Out of scope:
- WP-213 uninstall behavior, unresolved CLI flag or doctor decision, npm publishing, or making failed metrics pass by editing thresholds.

## Components Touched
- `docs/operations/` — Dashboard checklist and dated run record.
- Product code/tests only for defects discovered by the run, within existing WP scope.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- WP-207 workflow inference complete.
- WP-209 usage/cost complete.
- Both WP-210 destructive lifecycle tasks complete.
- WP-211 Dashboard UI integration complete.
- WP-212 role instruction/version task complete.
- WP-214 README task complete so final behavior and warnings can be checked together.
- WP-213 is intentionally absent; this task must not claim Phase 2a uninstall/doctor closure.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Use a disposable repo/trace store for destructive rehearsal; risk owner is hieu.nt10.
- Do not run `paseo daemon stop`; restart evidence follows the approved operational procedure and must not kill active work unexpectedly.
- A metric that misses its threshold is recorded `No` with the measurement; do not record PASS.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Real agents incur provider cost and user-owned archive/delete actions are irreversible; isolate fixtures and record scope before acting.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Checklist and run record exist and record D-1–D-11 individually.
- D-2–D-5 and D-8 use all five requests; D-6 uses three repos.
- D-9/D-11 include before/after filesystem snapshots proving no change outside `traces/`; D-10 compares provider-reported cost.
- Version update evidence shows store preservation.
- README comparison confirms all three required topics.

## Primary Proof
Dated real-daemon run record with metric table, screenshots/snapshots, provider comparison, update evidence, and linked fixture identifiers.

## Reversibility
Checklist/docs and defect fixes are revertible. Deletion/reassignment/archive actions are not; containment is disposable fixtures, previews, explicit confirmation, and R3 rehearsal ownership.

## Provenance

title: Make BM-REPORT bead-id lists robust and record incomplete lists
description:
## Objective
Make BM-REPORT bead-id list fields robust: ignore comment groups, expand `.N` shorthand ids, and record incomplete lists in a new `incompleteFields` on the parsed report and its schema.

## Context
In the live run of 2026-09-16 the Dashboard showed 2 created beads for `beadsCreated: x-gcj (epic), x-gcj.1, .2, .3` (9 were created) and 2 updated beads for `beadsUpdated: x-gcj.5 (b2 fix: no-logging AC)`, because the word `no-logging` matches `BEAD_ID`.

## Scope
In scope:
- A list parser returning `{ ids, complete }`; keep `parseBeadIds(raw): string[]` as a thin wrapper for existing callers.
- Parenthesised groups, evaluated before splitting: if every piece inside is a bead id, unwrap and keep the ids (existing test `(bm-wp-202-4xi.1).` must still pass); otherwise drop the whole group (`(epic)`, `(b2 fix: no-logging AC)`).
- Split on /[\s,;]+/ and strip punctuation exactly as today.
- Shorthand piece matching `^\.\d+(\.\d+)*$`: expand to ROOT + piece, where ROOT is the most recent full id earlier in the same list with ALL trailing `.<digits>` segments removed (`x-gcj.2.1, .2.2` → `x-gcj.2.2`; `x-gcj, x-gcj.1, .2` → `x-gcj.2`). No earlier full id → drop the piece and mark the list incomplete.
- A list is incomplete when any piece (after group handling) is neither a bead id, an expanded shorthand, nor an absent value (`none`, `-`, `n/a`, empty).
- Parsed report gains `incompleteFields: string[]` (canonical keys: beadsCreated, beadsUpdated, beadsClosed, beadsReady; the skillsUsed bead adds its own key).
- `parsedReportSchema` in plugin/shared/contracts.ts: add `incompleteFields: z.array(z.string()).default([])`.
Out of scope:
- The `skillsUsed` field (sibling bead), how counts and confidence are derived in traces.ts (separate bead), workflow steps, role files, re-parsing trace records already stored, any change to BEAD_ID (shell.ts also uses it) or to guardrail parsing (with or without a `polish` segment).

## Components Touched
- plugin/server/bm-report.ts and plugin/shared/bm-report.ts — identical except their one import line; keep it that way.
- plugin/shared/contracts.ts — parsedReportSchema.
- test/plugin-bm-report.test.ts — new cases; any test building ParsedReport literals may need the two new fields.
- A trace-store round-trip test (existing trace store test file).

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- none

## Assumptions / Constraints
- The trace store reads records through `traceRecordSchema.safeParse`, which drops undeclared keys; that is why the field goes into the schema. Defaults keep old records valid, so TRACE_STORE_SCHEMA_VERSION stays 1.
- The client chat cards import the shared copy; their display does not change.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Two parser copies drifting apart; run the same cases against both.
- `z.array(...).default([])` makes the inferred output type required; fix type errors in fixtures instead of loosening the schema.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `beadsCreated: x-gcj (epic), x-gcj.1, .2, .3` → [x-gcj, x-gcj.1, x-gcj.2, x-gcj.3], field not in incompleteFields.
- `beadsUpdated: x-gcj.5 (b2 fix: no-logging AC)` → [x-gcj.5].
- `beadsClosed: .2, x-a` → [x-a] and beadsClosed in incompleteFields.
- `beadsReady: x-a, and x-b` → [x-a, x-b] and beadsReady in incompleteFields.
- ``bm-wp-201-cp6.1`, (bm-wp-202-4xi.1).` still → both ids; `see the plan` → [] (and incomplete).
- Both parser copies give identical results for every new case.
- A trace record without `incompleteFields` parses through traceRecordSchema with []; a record with it round-trips unchanged.
- npm test, npm run typecheck and npm run typecheck:plugin pass.

## Primary Proof
`npx vitest run test/plugin-bm-report.test.ts` plus the trace-store round-trip test, then the full `npm test` and both typechecks.

## Reversibility
Revert the edits; stored records with the extra field stay readable by the old code (it drops unknown keys).

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-dashboard-implementation-plan-delta-20260917-workflow-skills.md#WP-215
Requirements: PRD Dashboard REQ-044 (b)(c), REQ-050 (b); PRD REQ-034 (b)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260917-workflow-skills.md §4.9, §5.1

title: Parse the new BM-REPORT field skillsUsed
description:
## Objective

## Context
The new Worker contract adds `skillsUsed: <skill names, comma-separated> | none` right after `buildAndTests` — the skills the Worker loaded for the request so far. The Dashboard's workflow steps and the Manager's skill supervision rely on it. Split from bm-wp-215-60a.1 so the new field and the list-parsing fix can be reviewed and reverted separately.

## Scope
In scope:
- Add `skillsused` → `skillsUsed` to the known-key map (never in `unparsedFields`).
- Parse with the same parenthesised-group handling and splitting as bead-id lists; keep pieces matching `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$` (case-insensitive, stored as written, trimmed, de-duplicated); absent values (`none`, `-`, `n/a`, empty) → []; any other piece adds `skillsUsed` to `incompleteFields`.

title: worker.md: run the workflow skills by tier and write atomic leaf beads
description:
## Objective
Rewrite the process parts of plugin/roles/worker.md so the Worker runs the workflow skills by tier, treats its own skill passes as self-improvement (never as Reviewer calls), and writes leaf beads to the converter's contract.

## Context
In the 2026-09-16 live run the Worker loaded only `feature-workflow`, created 8 thin beads by hand (only Acceptance Criteria + Provenance; one bead bundled routing, views, server wiring, config and tests) and never ran reviewing-plan, converting-plan-to-beads, polishing-beads or implementing-beads, because worker.md forbids "a review skill" and "a bead polish pass". The owner decided (2026-09-17): Large runs all five skills, Medium conditionally, Small keeps the fast path; skill passes are the Worker's and do not count against the review budget.

## Scope
In scope (rules to state in worker.md):
- Skill matrix. Small: no skills, fast path unchanged. Medium: affected document sections via feature-workflow; a plan only when the work needs one (several independent outcomes or a dependency graph) — with a plan run reviewing-plan, the plan-ready-for-beads gate and converting-plan-to-beads, without a plan create beads by hand to the leaf contract; polishing-beads always; implementing-beads for implementation. Large: full chain — documents → plan → reviewing-plan → plan-ready gate (PASS sets `Status: Active` and `Plan-ready: PASS — <date>`) → review batch b1 documents (plan included) → converting-plan-to-beads → polishing-beads → review batch b2 beads → user confirmation → implementing-beads → review batch b3 implementation → finished. Medium: documents (+plan path if any) → beads → polishing-beads → batch b1 plan (documents + beads) → implementing-beads → batch b2 implementation.
- worker.md still overrides skills on safety boundaries, the review budget, reporting, when to ask, and scope; skills decide HOW (document structure, gates, slicing, preflight).
- Replace "NEVER review your own work, use a review skill, or run a bead polish pass" with: a skill pass never replaces or counts as a Reviewer call, and the Worker never reviews a batch in place of the Reviewer. Remove "there is no polish pass".
- Skill-pass limits, not counted in the 1/4/6 review budget: reviewing-plan 1 pass per plan (and 1 per user-requested plan change); polishing-beads 1 pass per bead creation/update wave plus at most 1 targeted pass on beads it just split; converting-plan-to-beads once per plan.
- implementing-beads runs bead by bead, never with parallel sub-agents; its R2/R3 per-bead review requirement is satisfied by the single implementation review batch; choose beads only among this request's beads (by label), never another bead `bv --robot-next` suggests.
- Leaf contract for Medium/Large beads: Objective, Context, Scope (in/out), Components, Dependencies, Assumptions, Validation, Primary Proof, Reversibility, Provenance (converting-plan-to-beads reference/leaf-bead-checklist.md), keeping the lint headings (`## Acceptance Criteria`; bugs also `## Steps to Reproduce`; epics `## Success Criteria`). Small keeps its one-line bead.
- Atom rule: one independently reviewable and revertible outcome per leaf, tests with their outcome, never split by layer/file mechanically; never use file, line or bead counts as the criterion. implementing-beads' GO/SPLIT/BLOCK preflight runs before each bead. A SPLIT never deletes a bead and never makes a bead depend on its own children (with `br` a child is blocked while its parent is blocked, so the skill's coordinator pattern deadlocks): create SIBLING beads under the same parent, each with `Split-from: <id>`, move the original's dependency edges to the siblings that need them, then rewrite the original to the part it still owns or close it with the reason "split into <ids>".
Out of scope:
- Closing beads after their checks, reopening, and batches after finished (sibling bead); question rounds and the blocked format; report fields; the scratch-file rule; reviewer.md; manager.md.

## Components Touched
- plugin/roles/worker.md — RULES, Step 1 table, Step 3, Step 4, Review sections.
- test/roles-content.test.ts — worker.md describe block.
- plugin/server/worker-instructions.ts — regenerated, never hand-edited.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- none

## Assumptions / Constraints
- The file must still start with `## RULES`, keep hard rules in capitals, have no placeholder, and stay UNDER 240 lines (test/roles-content.test.ts enforces this; the owner asked for short files). Write each rule once; trim duplication instead of growing the file.
- Agent-facing text is English. Keep verbatim what code depends on: the BM-REPORT and BM-REVIEW blocks, the `BM-REVIEW STOPPED` line, `bm.*` label names, the mode-selection rules.
- test/roles-content.test.ts checks RULES, not prose: pin each new rule with one assertion; change an existing assertion only when the rule it pins was deliberately changed by the design delta, and say so in the test name.
- After editing, regenerate the embedded copy with `npm run generate:role-instructions` (the build also does it); the byte-match test must pass.
- Agents created before this change keep their old instructions; nothing to migrate.
- Review budget stays Small 1 / Medium 4 / Large 6 with the existing batch table; Manager's total table must keep matching.

## Risks / Gotchas
- The skills are long; tell the Worker to read only the parts it needs (SKILL.md plus the references the step uses).

## Acceptance Criteria
- worker.md states the tier/skill matrix and the Large and Medium order above.
- It states that skill passes do not count against the review budget and never replace a Reviewer call, with the three pass limits.
- It states the leaf contract for Medium/Large and the atom rule (no file/line/bead counts), and the Small one-line bead.
- It states the br split rule (siblings, never a bead depending on its own children).
- "NEVER review your own work, use a review skill, or run a bead polish pass" and "there is no polish pass" are gone; every other hard rule is still present.
- roles-content tests pin each of these; the file is under 240 lines; the embedded copy matches; npm test passes.

## Primary Proof
`npx vitest run test/roles-content.test.ts` plus the embedded-instructions byte-match test, then `npm test`.

## Reversibility
Revert worker.md, its tests and the regenerated file; agents created meanwhile keep the new text until the user starts new ones.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-dashboard-implementation-plan-delta-20260917-workflow-skills.md#WP-216
Requirements: PRD REQ-036 (a)(d), REQ-037 (as amended), REQ-032 (b)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260917-workflow-skills.md §3 Q1 Q2 Q8, §4.1, §4.2, §4.3, §7

Validated: roles-content 35 passed (new: skills by tier + order, leaf contract/atom/split; changed: override + no-polish assertions per delta), generate:role-instructions, npm test 85 files/1788 passed, typecheck + lint clean.

title: worker.md: mandatory decision and risk question rounds
description:
## Objective
Add the mandatory decision-and-risk question rounds to plugin/roles/worker.md and change the blocked format from one question to a numbered set.

## Context
In the 2026-09-16 live run the Worker changed three security decisions after a review (one broke the user's existing `.env`), added requirements nobody asked for, asked its first questions through Claude's AskUserQuestion box, and — when no answer came back — went on with its own recommended defaults. worker.md currently says "Raise a real risk in one sentence at most" and "Ask ONE clear question". The owner decided (2026-09-17) on mandatory rounds plus stop-and-ask on deviations.

## Scope
In scope (rules to state in worker.md):
- Mandatory rounds (Medium and Large): (1) on intake, before documents: open product and security decisions and the scope boundary; (2) after reviewing-plan: the open decisions the skill left for the user and the risks it found; (3) Large confirmation gate: a risk list — behaviour changes for existing users, config or secret changes, migrations, compatibility, security trade-offs, and every requirement added beyond the user's words — then ask to confirm. A round with nothing to ask is skipped; no token questions.
- Stop and ask before continuing (any tier) on: a deviation from approved documents; a behaviour change for existing users or a change to existing config/secrets; a requirement beyond the user's words; a security trade-off; a Reviewer finding that changes the approved design.

description:
## Objective
Rewrite plugin/roles/reviewer.md so the Reviewer uses stage criteria from the workflow skills, may run the repository's tests and throwaway probes without changing the repository, records the abuse cases it checked, and calibrates "blocking" to real defects.

## Context
In the 2026-09-16 live run the implementation review passed in 57 seconds and missed two security defects that an independent 4.5-minute review confirmed with scripts (an admin POST whose body arrives slowly still writes after the account is locked; long usernames make the login limiter hold ~300 MB). The document review, meanwhile, blocked on hardening the request did not need. reviewer.md names no skill and forbids every command except reads. The owner decided (2026-09-17): stage checklists plus running tests; no network, no installs, no writes to the repository.

## Scope
In scope (rules to state in reviewer.md):
- Stage criteria (read-only use; a skill that edits is used as criteria, never followed into editing):
  - documents: feature-workflow `checklists/prd-ready.md`, `checklists/design-ready.md`, `references/decision-gates.md`;
  - plan (Medium) or the plan inside documents (Large): `reviewing-plan` in its review-only mode (do not modify the plan) plus feature-workflow `checklists/plan-ready-for-beads.md`;
  - beads: converting-plan-to-beads `reference/leaf-bead-checklist.md` and polishing-beads `reference/readiness-checklist.md`, with the read commands `br show`, `br list`, `br dep tree`, `br ready`, `br lint`;
  - implementation: implementing-beads preflight, Hard Split Triggers and the R0–R3 risk table.
  - Skill files live under `~/.agents/skills`, `~/.codex/skills` or `~/.claude/skills`; a missing one goes to `notChecked` and the review continues under this file's rules.
- May run: the repository's existing test commands; lint or typecheck commands that write no files; throwaway scripts inside a directory it just created with `mktemp -d`.
- Still forbidden: network, installs, builds that write output, formatters, migrations, `br`/`bd` writes, any git state change, editing any file in the repository, creating/prompting/stopping agents.
- Run `git status --porcelain` before and after running commands; if it differs, say so in `notChecked` and do not clean up.
- Depth: a batch touching authentication, permissions, data or a public contract lists in `checked` the abuse and edge cases tried (authorization bypass, session revocation, check-then-write races, malformed input, unbounded resources, secret exposure).
- Blocking calibration: hardening beyond the request and the approved design is non-blocking unless it is an exploitable defect in what was built. At the beads stage, a Medium/Large leaf that bundles several independently reviewable or revertible outcomes, or lacks Primary Proof or Reversibility, is blocking.
- Format: with no findings write exactly `findings: none`; never a finding whose fields are all `none`.
Out of scope:
- worker.md and manager.md; the BM-REVIEW block itself (unchanged); the stop notice handling (unchanged).

## Components Touched
- plugin/roles/reviewer.md — RULES, "What you review", "Blocking or not", "Result".

## Assumptions / Constraints

- Regenerate the embedded copy with `npm run generate:role-instructions`; the byte-match test must pass. Agents created before the change keep their old instructions.
- The Reviewer runs in the provider's automatic mode without full or network access (unchanged); the new command permissions are behavioural only.
- `br` read commands were verified on 2026-09-17 not to write `.beads/` files.

## Risks / Gotchas

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Dashboard ready count uses the latest report and incomplete lists lower confidence
description:
## Objective
Make the Dashboard's bead counts truthful: `ready` comes from the latest report that carries `beadsReady`, and a count whose field was reported incomplete carries confidence `inferred`.

## Context
In the 2026-09-16 live run the final trace showed ready = 3 although the finished report said `beadsReady: none`, because `beadActionsOf` (plugin/server/traces.ts) takes the union of every report; and every count was labelled `exact` merely because a report existed, even when the list could not be fully read.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Build a trace with a `beads-done` report `beadsReady: a-1, a-2, a-3` and a later `finished` report `beadsReady: none`.
2. Call `summarise` / `detail`.
3. Observe beadCounts.ready = 3 with confidence exact.

title: Link Manager turns by the Continue <requestId> relay prompt
description:
## Objective
Link a Manager turn to its request when the Manager's relay prompt starts with `Continue <requestId>`, so a user's follow-up no longer shows as a separate provisional request row.

## Context
manager.md tells the Manager to resume a Worker with `Continue <requestId>.` plus the user's words. The collector (plugin/server/collector.ts `buildRecord`) reads only user and assistant message text, and `REQUEST_ID_PATTERN` needs a literal `requestId:` label, so in the 2026-09-16 live run every user answer sat in its own "unknown" row until the Worker's next report.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Record a Manager turn whose only inbound message is a user answer and whose only tool call is `mcp__paseo__send_agent_prompt` with `input.prompt` = "Continue req-20260916T154448Z.\n\nĐồng ý…".
2. Rebuild traces for the workspace before any later report.
3. Observe a trace row with requestId null and state unknown.

## Scope
In scope:
- In `buildRecord`, for tool_call items whose name is `send_agent_prompt` (compare the part after the last `__`, or the whole name) with a string `detail.input.prompt`, match `^\s*Continue\s+(req-\d{8}T\d{6}Z)\b`.
- Use the match as the record's requestId only as the LAST fallback: label → reports → inbound prompt text → this relay id.
- Apply to Manager records (role manager) only.
Out of scope:
- Bare ids in Manager replies (they can cite other requests), the "next named request" folding rule, the Worker/Reviewer bare-id majority rule, re-linking records already stored.

## Components Touched
- plugin/server/collector.ts — `buildRecord` (requestId chain near line 384).
- test/plugin-collector.test.ts and test/plugin-traces-reconstruct.test.ts — new cases.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Live timeline shape (verified on the 2026-09-16 run): item.type `tool_call`, name `mcp__paseo__send_agent_prompt`, detail `{ type: "unknown", input: { agentId, prompt }, output }`.
- No new evidence kind; the contracts enum stays as is.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The reproduction yields a record with requestId req-20260916T154448Z and the rebuilt workspace has no provisional row for that turn.
- A prompt with `req-…` in the middle of a sentence does not set requestId.
- A Worker/Reviewer record with such a tool call is unaffected.
- A record that already has a requestId from a label or report keeps it.
- Existing collector and reconstruct tests pass; npm test and both typechecks pass.

## Primary Proof

## Reversibility

title: Price trace totals per record model and flag unpriced tokens
description:
## Objective
Price a trace's total usage per record model, so the total equals the sum of the per-agent costs and tokens from models without a price are excluded and named in a notice.

## Context
`summariseUsage` (plugin/server/traces.ts ~768) sums tokens across every record of a trace and prices the sum with one model — the model of the last record. In the 2026-09-16 live run the total was $17.71 while Manager $0.68 + Worker $14.55 = $15.23: the Codex Reviewer tokens were priced as claude-opus-5. If a Reviewer record is last, the whole total becomes unavailable instead.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Build a trace with records of model claude-opus-5 and records of model gpt-5.6-sol (not in the price table), the gpt record last.
2. Call `summarise` with the real `priceUsage`.
3. Observe a total that prices the gpt tokens at opus rates (or no cost at all if the order is reversed).

## Scope
In scope:
- Total cost = sum over records (or over per-model groups) priced with each record's own model.
- Total `model`: that model when all records with tokens share one; otherwise null.
- Total `costUsd`: sum of the priced parts; null when no part is priced. `costBasis`: `estimated` when at least one part is priced, else `unavailable`.
- Token counts in the total stay the plain sums.
- When tokens from unpriced models exist, add the notice `Cost excludes <n> tokens from models without a price: <model, …>.` to the trace's summary and detail notices (n = input + cached + output tokens of those models).
- The client overview, which sums `trace.usage.costUsd`, then becomes correct without client changes.
Out of scope:
- Provider-reported cost (`totalCostUsd` deltas) — deferred by the design; the price table; per-agent usage (already priced per agent).

## Components Touched
- plugin/server/traces.ts — `summariseUsage` and where summary/detail notices are assembled.
- plugin/server/cost.ts — only if a helper is needed (keep `priceUsage` behaviour for single-model input).
- test/plugin-traces-detail.test.ts, test/plugin-cost.test.ts, test/plugin-dashboard-model.test.ts — update expectations that assumed single-model pricing.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- none

## Assumptions / Constraints
- `usageSchema` does not change; the notice uses the existing `notices` arrays.
- Cost stays an estimate (Dashboard design §9).

## Acceptance Criteria
- The reproduction yields total cost = opus part only, model null, costBasis estimated, and the notice naming gpt-5.6-sol with the right token count.
- Order of records does not change the result.
- A single-model trace yields exactly today's numbers and no notice.
- A trace with only unpriced tokens yields costUsd null, costBasis unavailable and the notice.
- Total cost equals the sum of per-agent costs for the same trace.
- npm test and both typechecks pass.

## Primary Proof
Focused vitest cases for `summariseUsage`/`summarise`/`detail`, then `npm test`.

## Reversibility
Revert the traces/cost changes and tests; nothing is persisted.

title: Derive convert, polish and implement steps from skill evidence; fix the polish-skipped rule
description:
## Objective
Derive `convert_to_beads`, `polish_beads` and `implement` from skill evidence, stop reading a guardrail without a polish segment as "polish skipped", and update which tiers may skip which step.

## Context
Since 2026-09-16 the guardrail line has no `polish` segment and `polish_beads` is treated as skipped for every tier (`(polish ?? 0) === 0` and `SKIPPABLE_BY_TIER`). Polish is back for Medium and Large (owner decision 2026-09-17), so that rule now hides real omissions. `implement` is exact only on the retired phase `bead-implemented`.

## Scope
In scope (plugin/server/workflow-steps.ts):
- convert_to_beads: keep today's signals; add exact when `skillsUsed` contains `converting-plan-to-beads`, inferred on `skill` evidence `converting-plan-to-beads`. A missing skill never makes it skipped (hand-made Medium beads are valid).
- polish_beads: exact when `skillsUsed` contains `polishing-beads`, or an old guardrail says `polish n/max` with n ≥ 1; inferred on `skill` evidence `polishing-beads` or `br update` on ≥ 2 distinct beads (as today). Exact negative ONLY when a guardrail explicitly says `polish 0`, or a `finished` report has a non-empty `skillsUsed` without `polishing-beads` (skipped + note naming the skill). A guardrail without a polish segment is no evidence.
- implement: exact on `phase: bead-implemented` (old reports) or `skillsUsed` containing `implementing-beads`; inferred from file evidence as today. A missing skill never makes it skipped.
- `SKIPPABLE_BY_TIER`: Small prd, design, adr, plan, review_plan, polish_beads; Medium review_plan only; Large none (review_plan entries come from the previous bead — keep them).
Out of scope:
- Absolute-path handling in the implement/doc rules (next bead), the review_plan rule itself, role files.

## Components Touched
- plugin/server/workflow-steps.ts — findStep cases and SKIPPABLE_BY_TIER; header comment about "no tier polishes".
- test/plugin-workflow-steps.test.ts.
- docs comment in code only; design docs are updated by the documentation bead.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- The review_plan step bead (WP-218) must be done first: same file, same table, and its skippable entries.
- The `skillsUsed` parser bead (WP-215) provides the field.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Keep D-5: an absent signal is unknown, never skipped, except via the tier table.
- `parseGuardrail` returns `polish: null` when the segment is absent; distinguish null from 0.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Guardrail `batch b1 reviews 1/1; total 1/4; userAllowedExtra 0` in a Medium trace with no other polish signal → polish_beads unknown (was skipped).
- Old guardrail with `polish 0/1` → skipped exact; `polish 1/1` → done exact.
- `skillsUsed` with polishing-beads → done exact; a Large finished report whose skillsUsed lacks it → skipped with a note.
- Medium finished report with beadsCreated and skillsUsed lacking converting-plan-to-beads → convert_to_beads done.
- `skillsUsed: implementing-beads` → implement done exact.
- Small with no signal → polish_beads skipped; Medium with no signal → polish_beads unknown.

title: Normalise absolute file evidence against the workspace directory
description:
## Objective
Normalise absolute file-evidence paths against the workspace directory so documentation writes are not counted as implementation and writes outside the workspace are ignored.

## Context
The collector stores file evidence as the tool reported it — absolute paths (`/Users/…/docs/design/x.md`, even `~/.claude/projects/…/memory/…`). `DOC_PREFIX` compares with `docs/…`, so the implement step counted document writes, and the documentation steps never matched their inferred signal.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Build a trace whose only file evidence is `/ws/docs/design/x.md` with workspace directory `/ws`.
2. Run `inferWorkflowSteps`.
3. Observe implement = done (inferred) and design without the inferred file signal.

## Scope
In scope:
- `handleTracesGet` (plugin/server/dashboard-rpc.ts) passes the workspace `directory` it already has into `inferWorkflowSteps` context (e.g. `workspaceDir`).
- In workflow-steps: an absolute path under `workspaceDir` becomes workspace-relative before the `docs/`, `docs/<kind>/` and `.beads/` checks; a relative path is used as is; an absolute path outside the workspace, or any absolute path when `workspaceDir` is null, is not evidence for implement or document steps. `~`-prefixed paths count as outside.
Out of scope:
- Rewriting stored evidence; the collector; other steps.

## Components Touched
- plugin/server/workflow-steps.ts — InferContext, DOC_PREFIX matching, implement inferred rule.
- plugin/server/dashboard-rpc.ts — pass the directory.
- test/plugin-workflow-steps.test.ts, test/plugin-dashboard-rpc.test.ts if it asserts the call.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- The skill-evidence bead of WP-218 must be done first (same rules in the same file).

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Path comparison uses the resolved directory with a trailing separator so `/ws2/src` is not inside `/ws`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The reproduction yields design done/inferred and implement not done from that path.
- `/ws/src/a.js` → implement done/inferred; `/ws/.beads/issues.jsonl` → not implement.
- `/other/src/a.js` and `~/.claude/x.md` → ignored.
- `workspaceDir` null → absolute paths ignored; relative `src/a.js` still counts.
- npm test and both typechecks pass.

## Primary Proof
`npx vitest run test/plugin-workflow-steps.test.ts test/plugin-dashboard-rpc.test.ts`, then `npm test`.

## Reversibility
Revert the two source files and tests.

title: Independent review of the full workflow-skills diff
description:

title: Install the updated payload on the owner's daemon and confirm it runs
description:
## Objective
Install the updated payload on the owner's Paseo daemon (same version reinstall) and confirm the plugin runs the new instructions.

## Context
Role instructions and Dashboard code only take effect once the daemon loads the new payload. The owner lets Claude run acceptance on the real daemon (orchestration-acceptance runbook practice).

## Scope
In scope:
- Back up `~/.paseo/config.json` to the run's evidence folder before installing.
- Build and reinstall the current version from the working tree the way previous acceptance runs did (same-version reinstall auto-reloads the plugin).
- Check `paseo plugin ls --json` shows `paseo-bm` with `status: running`, and that the installed `roles/*.md` match the working tree.
Out of scope:
- Publishing, version bumps, daemon restart or stop (never), plugin removal.

## Components Touched
- ~/.paseo-bm/plugin/<version>/ (install home), ~/.paseo/config.json (by the installer only).

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- The independent review bead (WP-220) must be closed first.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Check `status`, never `enabled`. Never run `paseo daemon restart` or `stop`.
- If the plugin is not `running` after install: stop, keep the state, report to the owner; do not experiment on the daemon.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Backup file exists; `paseo plugin ls --json` → paseo-bm running at the install-home path; `diff -r plugin/roles ~/.paseo-bm/plugin/<version>/roles` is empty.

## Primary Proof
The backup path, the `paseo plugin ls --json` output and the empty diff.

## Reversibility
Reinstall the previous payload from the working tree state before this delta and restore config from the backup if needed.

title: Run one real Large request and write the acceptance record
description:
## Objective
Run one real Large request through Beads Manager on a fresh copy of the Team Portal baseline and record evidence that the new contract works.

## Context
Content tests only prove the instructions say the right thing. The 2026-09-16 run (kit in ~/bm-demo/20260916/kit: send.mjs sends like the app, watch.mjs watches agents, timeline.mjs, rpc.mjs) is the baseline to compare against.

## Scope
In scope:
- New run directory ~/bm-demo/20260917 with a fresh Team Portal baseline, decoy `.env`, a new Paseo workspace, Manager via `manager.ensure`, Manager set to bypassPermissions (owner decision for acceptance runs).
- Request: "Xây dựng hệ thống quản lý user và màn hình login cho Team Portal." Answer questions as the user; never auto-allow AskUserQuestion; record every answer.
- Collect: agents and modes, timelines, bead list, traces.list/traces.get, events, permission decisions.

title: Fix the 13 approved non-blocking findings of the independent review
description:
## Objective
Fix the 13 non-blocking findings of the independent review bm-wp-220-nvk.1 that the owner chose to fix (2026-09-17), before the payload is installed.

## Context
The review of the whole workflow-skills delta found 3 blocking problems (fixed by reopening their beads) and 15 non-blocking ones. The owner decided: fix 13, record 2 without fixing. Five of the 13 are contradictions in the role instructions that could derail the live acceptance run.

## Scope
In scope (each with a test or content assertion):
1. worker.md: the SMALL FAST PATH follows Step 4's order — make the change → cheapest check → close with evidence → one review → reopen on a blocking finding → finished.
2. worker.md: `notifyOnFinish: false` is for BM-REPORT messages only; Reviewer create and re-review calls keep the default so the verdict wakes the Worker.
3. worker.md: "Keep reports and replies to a few lines" has an exception for the numbered question list.
4. manager.md: "If the user answered the Worker directly" becomes "If the user tells you they already answered the Worker".
5. reviewer.md: the Reviewer deletes its `mktemp -d` directory before answering.
6. workflow-steps.ts `workspacePath`: relative paths are normalised (`src/../docs/x.md` → `docs/x.md`) and a path that escapes the workspace (`../outside/a.js`) is not evidence.
7. bm-report.ts (both copies): a list or skillsUsed value longer than 8,000 characters is cut to 8,000 before parsing and the field is marked incomplete (the parser is quadratic on crafted input: 40 KB of nested parentheses took 1.6 s).
8. traces.ts `usageOfTrace`: group by the model id without a provider prefix (`bm-worker/claude-opus-5` ≡ `claude-opus-5`); a trace whose usage records carry zero tokens keeps the previous result (priced total, model kept) instead of "cost unavailable".
9. traces.ts per-agent usage (`usageOfAgent`): priced per model through `usageOfTrace`, so an agent that switched models is not priced wholly at its last model.
10. collector.ts relay pattern: tolerate markdown around the keyword and the id (`**Continue** req-…`, `Continue \`req-…\``), still anchored at the start.
11. dashboard-rpc.ts: when Paseo no longer lists the workspace, pass the trace store's `lastKnownDirectory` as the workflow table's workspace directory (design delta §5.5 names that source).
12. test/plugin-traces-detail.test.ts: the "total equals the sum of the per-agent costs" test compares with `detail().usageByAgent` from the product, not a recomputation.
13. README.md: the fixed question moments are stated for Medium and Large requests.
Out of scope (recorded, not done): `ready` cannot tell a missing `beadsReady` line from `none`; id-shaped words outside parentheses still count as bead ids (predates the delta); a `.N` shorthand inside a dropped comment group is dropped without the incomplete flag.

## Components Touched
- plugin/roles/worker.md, manager.md, reviewer.md (+ regenerated *-instructions.ts), test/roles-content.test.ts
- plugin/server/workflow-steps.ts, bm-report.ts, plugin/shared/bm-report.ts, traces.ts, collector.ts, dashboard-rpc.ts and their tests
- README.md

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- none (the blocking fixes are already closed)

## Assumptions / Constraints
- No new scope: every item corrects behaviour the delta already specified or makes its instructions consistent.
- worker.md stays under 270 lines, reviewer.md and manager.md under 240.
- Two parser copies stay identical except their import line.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each of the 13 items is covered by a new or updated test/assertion that fails without the change (negative control for the code items).
- npm test, typecheck, typecheck:plugin and lint exit 0; role files within their line limits; embedded instructions regenerated.

## Primary Proof
The focused vitest runs for the touched files plus the negative controls, then the full `npm run verify`.

## Reversibility
Revert the listed files; nothing is persisted.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-dashboard-implementation-plan-delta-20260917-workflow-skills.md#WP-220
Requirements: plan-delta exit condition 1; review bm-wp-220-nvk.1 findings N2–N15 (owner decision 2026-09-17)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260917-workflow-skills.md §4, §5
close_reason: Fixed the 13 owner-approved non-blocking review findings: worker.md Small fast path order, notifyOnFinish:false for reports only, few-lines exception for question lists; manager.md 'if the user tells you they already answered'; reviewer.md delete mktemp dir; README question moments for Medium/Large; workspacePath normalises relative paths and rejects ../ escapes; MAX_LIST_CHARS=8000 cap (both parser copies) -> incomplete; usageOfTrace groups provider-qualified ids and keeps zero-token results; usageOfAgent priced per model; relay regex tolerates markdown; evidenceDirectory falls back to trace-store lastKnownDirectory (workflow table only); cost test compares detail().usageByAgent. Plus the two regressions the one re-review found in these fixes: an unreadable latest finished skillsUsed now blocks an older report's negative, and the cap drops the id it cut through. Each code item has a test whose negative control fails without the fix; the one re-review (bm-wp-220-nvk.1) confirmed no regressions for the 13 items; the last two regression fixes were not re-reviewed (review budget). Validated: npm run verify exit 0 (85 files/1845 tests, build success); role files 263/135/139 lines; br lint and dep cycles clean. Recorded, not fixed (owner): ready vs missing line, id-shaped words outside parentheses, shorthand inside a dropped group (design delta §7, plan R-3).

title: worker.md and reviewer.md: never bend a check to close a bead
description:
## Objective
Add the two rules that stop a bead from being closed on a check that did not pass: never edit a test or a bead's acceptance criteria to make a check go green, and read the check's own result before closing.

## Context
While implementing the workflow-skills delta, the runner (Claude) made both mistakes a Worker can make. In `bm-wp-215-60a.2` a test was rewritten to match the parser instead of the parser being fixed to match the bead's acceptance case — only the independent review caught it. In `bm-wp-216-v23.2` the bead was closed while `npm test` was red, because the close command was chained after a `grep` that still matched. Nothing in `worker.md` forbids either, and `reviewer.md` does not call a weakened test blocking. Owner asked for these process holes to be fixed (2026-09-17, design delta §4.10 rules 4 and 5).

## Scope
In scope:
- worker.md RULES: **NEVER change a test, an assertion, or a bead's Acceptance Criteria to make a check pass.** A red check means the code is wrong or the bead is wrong: fix the code, or stop and ask the user (the `blocked` path). Changing a test is allowed only when the bead itself asks for it, and the report says so.
- worker.md Step 4: before closing a bead, read the check's own result (exit status and the summary line); a command whose output shows failures is not evidence. Never put the close command in the same chained command line as the check that is supposed to prove it.
- reviewer.md "Blocking or not": a test, assertion or acceptance criterion weakened or deleted so that a check passes is a **blocking** finding.
- Both rules apply to every tier, including the Small fast path.
Out of scope:
- The three rules of bm-wp-221-ain9 (Manager wording, temp-dir deletion, review counting); any change to budgets, tiers or report moments.

## Components Touched
- plugin/roles/worker.md (RULES, Step 4), plugin/roles/reviewer.md (Blocking or not), regenerated *-instructions.ts, test/roles-content.test.ts.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- none

## Assumptions / Constraints
- worker.md stays under 270 lines, reviewer.md under 240; `## RULES` first; regenerate with `npm run generate:role-instructions`.
- Wording must not clash with "Prove a change with the cheapest check that actually proves it".

## Acceptance Criteria
- worker.md forbids editing a test/assertion/acceptance criterion to make a check pass, and names the two allowed answers (fix the code, or ask).
- worker.md requires reading the check result before closing, and forbids chaining the close command onto the check.
- reviewer.md lists a weakened or deleted test as blocking.
- roles-content tests pin all three; line limits hold; embedded instructions match; npm run verify exits 0.

## Primary Proof
`npx vitest run test/roles-content.test.ts` plus the byte-match test, then `npm run verify`.

## Reversibility
Revert the two role files, their tests and the regenerated files.

## Provenance
Source: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260917-workflow-skills.md#410-sửa-sau-lượt-nghiệm-thu-2026-09-17
Requirements: PRD REQ-022, REQ-024, REQ-037 (evidence before closing)
Design refs: design delta §4.10 rules 4 and 5; run record docs/operations/paseo-bm-workflow-skills-run-20260917.md
close_reason: Re-closed after the one re-review of this batch: the escape hatch now reads 'Change a test only when the bead ALREADY asked for that change before you ran the check; rewriting the bead to allow it is the same violation', and the destructive rule reads '`rm -rf` on anything you did not create yourself' so a Worker may delete its own mktemp -d dir in any phase while other files stay protected. Reviewer verdict: hatch closed, no weakening, no regression. Validated: npm run verify exit 0 read from its exit status (85 files, 1846 tests, build ok), roles-content 45 passed with the updated and new assertions, generate:role-instructions run; worker.md 273/280 lines. Suggestion (not done): the dropped ', and report it.' obligation for a legitimate test change — filesChanged already shows the file.

comments.author: hieunguyentrung
comments.text: Reopened by the review of this bead: 'Change a test only when the bead asks for it' is a loophole (the Worker writes its own beads, so it can make the bead ask after the check went red). Also the rm -rf wording covers only files created 'for the bead', not a temp dir created during the documents phase.

title: Role instruction fixes from the 2026-09-17 acceptance run
description:
## Objective
Correct three role-instruction gaps the 2026-09-17 acceptance run exposed: the Manager guessing the Worker's next step, the Worker leaving a `mktemp -d` directory behind, and the Worker over-counting its review calls.

## Context
The acceptance run of the workflow-skills delta (docs/operations/paseo-bm-workflow-skills-run-20260917.md) passed, but the timelines show three deviations that the instructions do not prevent. None of them is a code defect; all three are wording gaps in `plugin/roles/*.md`.

## Scope
In scope:
1. manager.md: after a `beads-done` report of a **Large** request, the Manager must not say the Worker is starting to implement — that tier waits for the user's confirmation. State it with the existing "never guess" rule (observed 01:30:43: "Worker chuyển sang viết code", corrected by the Worker's `blocked` report 10 s later).
2. worker.md: a `mktemp -d` directory must be deleted as soon as the work that needed it is done, and in any case before the next report (observed: the bead-draft directory /var/folders/…/tmp.6Ziug02DLj survived the whole request, while the smoke-test directories were removed).
3. worker.md: define the review counter exactly — one call is one message sent to a Reviewer (the creation prompt or a re-review prompt); a batch's re-review is one call, not two (observed: 4 real calls — b1 first + re-review, b2 first, b3 first — reported as `total 5/6`).
Out of scope:
- The Reviewer's inability to run HTTP tests under the Codex `auto` sandbox (needs an owner decision; see the run record §5).
- Any code change; any change to the budgets, the report moments or the batch table.

## Components Touched
- plugin/roles/manager.md, plugin/roles/worker.md (+ regenerated *-instructions.ts), test/roles-content.test.ts.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- none

## Assumptions / Constraints
- worker.md stays under 270 lines, manager.md under 240; `## RULES` stays first; regenerate with `npm run generate:role-instructions`.
- Agents created before the change keep their instructions.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Item 3 changes only the definition, not the numbers: Small 1, Medium 4, Large 6 stay as they are.

## Acceptance Criteria
- manager.md states that a Large request waits for the user after `beads-done`, and that the Manager does not announce implementation before the user confirms.
- worker.md states when a temp directory must be deleted (as soon as it is no longer needed, at the latest before the next report).
- worker.md defines a review call as one message to a Reviewer and gives the b1 first + re-review = 2 example.
- roles-content tests pin all three; line limits hold; embedded instructions match; npm test, lint and both typechecks pass.

## Primary Proof
`npx vitest run test/roles-content.test.ts` plus the byte-match test, then `npm run verify`.

## Reversibility
Revert the two role files, their tests and the regenerated files.

## Provenance
Source: docs/operations/paseo-bm-workflow-skills-run-20260917.md#5
Requirements: PRD REQ-034, REQ-037 (counting), REQ-026 (temp files)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260917-workflow-skills.md §4.5, §4.6, §4.8
close_reason: Three acceptance-run gaps fixed: manager.md reports beads-done as it is and, for Large, says the Worker waits for the user (never announces implementation first); worker.md deletes a mktemp -d directory as soon as the work needing it is done, at the latest before the next report; worker.md defines one review call as one message sent to a Reviewer (first + re-review = 2, pass-first-time = 1) for the guardrail counter. Validated: npm run verify exit 0 (85 files, 1845 tests, build ok) read from its exit status; roles-content 44 passed with three new assertions; generate:role-instructions run; worker.md 267/270, manager.md 142/240 lines. Recorded in design delta §4.10 rows 1-3.

title: Rewrite roles-content tests to check behaviour, not wording
description:
## Objective
Turn `test/roles-content.test.ts` into a two-layer suite — verbatim pins for what code reads, one intent-level assertion per hard limit — that is green against the three role files **as they are today**, before any of them is rewritten.

## Context
The suite is 555 lines and pins nearly every sentence of the three role files. Its own header comment warns that this would make the next simplification expensive, and that is exactly what happened: the owner asked on 2026-09-17 to cut the case-by-case prohibitions, and every cut would turn several assertions red for wording reasons alone. This bead removes that coupling first, so that when the files are rewritten a red test means a behaviour was lost, not that a sentence moved.

## Scope
In scope:
- Rewrite the assertions so each hard limit is checked by intent (alternation of a few interchangeable keywords), matched against the WHOLE file text rather than inside one `## ` section, because design delta §4.3 moves many sentences out of `## RULES` into the steps.
- Keep verbatim pins for: the `BM-REPORT` block (all field names, their order, `skillsUsed` directly after `buildAndTests`), the `BM-REVIEW` block, the `BM-REVIEW STOPPED` line, the `STOP: The Beads Worker...` notice, label names `bm.role` / `bm.requestId` / `bm.batchId` / `bm.version`, `feature:<slug>`, `Continue <requestId>.`, provider strings `bm-worker/` and `bm-reviewer/`, the review budget numbers 1 / 4 / 6, the report phase names, `Plan-ready: PASS`.
- Keep the structural checks that already exist: `## RULES` is the first heading, no placeholders, the Large chain order, the skills-by-tier table, the tier ordering rule.
- `section()` survives only for machine-read blocks and for order-inside-a-section assertions.
- Before the first write of this delta, copy `plugin/roles/*.md` and `test/roles-content.test.ts` into a directory created with `mktemp -d` and keep it until the last bead of the delta closes. Nothing here is committed and `git checkout` would swallow seven earlier deltas, so that copy is the revert path this phase approves, for this bead and for the three rewrites after it.
Out of scope:
- Any edit to `plugin/roles/*.md` — this bead must not change a single byte there.
- The 240-line limit and the prohibition budget: both are false today and land in the last work package.

## Components Touched
- test/roles-content.test.ts

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- none

## Assumptions / Constraints
- The suite must pass both before and after the role files are rewritten; that double pass is the evidence it follows behaviour.
- Coverage of hard limits stays complete: every limit in design delta §4.2 has exactly one assertion.

## Risks / Gotchas
- An intent assertion written too loosely (for example matching the single word `never`) would pass on any text. Each one must name the object of the limit — secrets, push, destroy, green check, decide — not just the negation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `npx vitest run test/roles-content.test.ts` is green with `git diff --stat plugin/roles/` empty.
- Every hard limit of design delta §4.2 (W1-W5, R1-R4, M1-M5) has one assertion that does not depend on the current sentence.
- Every machine-read contract listed in scope is still pinned verbatim.
- The phase copy exists and holds the four pre-rewrite files.
- No assertion for a moving rule is scoped to a `## ` section.

## Primary Proof
`npx vitest run test/roles-content.test.ts` green while `plugin/roles/` is untouched, plus the negative control below.

## Reversibility
Single test file; restore it from the phase copy this bead creates.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260917b-simplify-roles.md#wp-222
Requirements: PRD REQ-032(b)(d)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260917b-simplify-roles.md §4.6
close_reason: Re-closed after fixing blocking finding B7 of the b1 documents review. B7: the reviewer and manager hard-limit assertions were still near-verbatim pins of the old sentences (NEVER write documents, create/update/close beads, or change code / NEVER archive or delete any agent / NEVER read another agent's conversation / NEVER change beads / NEVER touch git), so rewriting those two files would have turned about ten assertions red for wording alone inside the bead licensed to loosen them. All of them are now keyword alternations, like W1-W5 already were. Added a new helper about(text, anchor, window, ...required) for rules that are an AND about one subject, so an alternation cannot pass on its easiest half. Also added the three anchors the same review found missing: a migration on real data (B1), the four verbs revert/reformat/stage/discard for changes already in the tree (B2), and the tracker-guard override --force (B3). Two anchors were themselves defective and were fixed here: 'already in the working tree' was coupled to my own draft wording (replaced by four verb rules), and about(manager, 'agent') passed even with the prohibition deleted because manager.md explains archiving elsewhere (replaced by a precise alternation). Validated, each read from its own exit status: npx vitest run test/roles-content.test.ts = 53 passed with all three role files byte-identical to the pre-rewrite copy (diff -q); npm run typecheck exit 0; npm run lint exit 0. Negative control, 9 mutations in total: worker W3 secrets, worker W4 bent check, reviewer R2 network/install, manager M3 conversation, worker B1 migration, worker B2 reformat/stage/discard, worker B3 --force, reviewer R1 archive/delete, manager M4 archive/delete — each turned exactly 1 test red, each file restored byte-identical. title: worker.md: five hard limits, and the workflow as its own section
description:
## Objective
Rewrite `plugin/roles/worker.md` so its `## RULES` section is five hard limits stated by CLASS of behaviour, and the rest of the file reads as the order of work and how to do it.

## Context
On 2026-09-17 the owner said the Worker and Reviewer instructions prohibit far too much, case by case, and that telling an agent what to do — and letting the other roles carry their part — beats adding another ban. `worker.md` holds 37 prohibition words and 19 bullets in RULES (19% of the file), mixing real safety boundaries (`NEVER read secret files`) with tool trivia (`NEVER use SendMessage`) and style (`Keep reports to a few lines`). Seven consecutive deltas each added lines to the same block and none merged them. The workflow chains an agent needs most sit buried in Step 3 between the label rules and the lint-heading rules.

## Scope
In scope:
- `## RULES` becomes exactly the five hard limits of design delta §4.2: (W1) nothing leaves this workspace without an explicit yes, (W2) never destroy what you did not create, (W3) never read or copy secrets, (W4) never make a check look green, (W5) never decide what only the user can decide. Each limit names a class and gives at most four examples in parentheses.
- Every other current rule moves to the place design delta §4.3 assigns it, written as an instruction rather than a ban: `SendMessage` to the report section, `AskUserQuestion` to the questions section, `git status` and the `mktemp -d` temp-directory guidance to Step 4, report length and language to a short "How you talk" section, the frozen-document / scope / bead-deletion triggers to the stop-and-ask list.
- Pull the Large / Medium / Small chains out of Step 3 into their own section, placed directly after the tier table.
- Merge the old Step 2 (labels) into the documents-and-beads step.
- Drop the six items of design delta §4.4 that another role already blocks by reading.
- Keep the file in English (repo language rule); the Vietnamese section names in design delta §4.5 are descriptions, not text to copy.
Out of scope:
- Any change to what the rules decide: tiers, the 1/4/6 budget, batch definitions, the three asking moments, the report moments, the leaf-bead contract, the `BM-REPORT` block, agent creation.
- reviewer.md and manager.md.

## Risks / Gotchas

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every row of design delta §4.3 (worker table) is satisfied: the rule is either inside a hard limit, or present as an instruction in the named section, or listed in §4.4 as dropped.

title: reviewer.md: four hard limits, and what you may run stated positively
description:
## Objective
Rewrite `plugin/roles/reviewer.md` so its `## RULES` section is four hard limits, and everything a Reviewer may actually run is written as positive guidance in the section about how it checks.

## Context
`reviewer.md` opens with eight prohibition bullets that enumerate cases rather than classes: seven git verbs, five kinds of writing command, agent operations, file edits, bead edits. All of them say the same thing once the class is named — a Reviewer changes nothing. The owner asked on 2026-09-17 for exactly this: ban the big thing, not each instance. The single positive bullet in that block (`YOU MAY RUN: ...`) is the one an agent needs most and is buried at position five.

## Scope
In scope:
- `## RULES` becomes the four hard limits of design delta §4.2: (R1) you change nothing — no file, bead, git or agent change, having a tool is not permission, a check that would change something is skipped and named in `notChecked`; (R2) nothing leaves this machine — no network, installs or downloads; (R3) never read secrets, and report an added secret as blocking without repeating its value; (R4) one batch, one result — review only the scope given, never ask for another round.
- Move `YOU MAY RUN` and the `git status --porcelain` before/after check into the section on how you check, written positively and unchanged in substance.
- Drop the two enumerations of design delta §4.4 (five kinds of writing command, seven git verbs); R1 covers them by class.
- Keep the file in English.
Out of scope:
- The stage-criteria table, the sensitive-batch abuse list, the blocking / non-blocking classification, the `BM-REVIEW` block and the stop line: content unchanged.
- worker.md and manager.md.

- plugin/roles/reviewer.md, plugin/server/reviewer-instructions.ts (regenerated), test/roles-content.test.ts (only if an intent anchor no longer matches)

- Run `npm run generate:role-instructions` before closing.

## Risks / Gotchas
- R1 must keep the clause that a tool being available is not permission to use it: the Reviewer runs in a mode that can hold write tools, and that sentence is the only thing standing between it and a "helpful" fix.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `## RULES` contains exactly the four hard limits and nothing else.
- Every row of design delta §4.3 (reviewer table) is satisfied, or listed in §4.4 as dropped.

title: Tighten the role-file line limit to 240 and add a prohibition budget
description:
## Objective
Lower the role-file line limit to 240 for all three files and add a prohibition budget so a later delta cannot quietly grow the bans back.

## Context
`worker.md` needed two limit increases during the previous delta (240 to 270, then 270 to 280), each one asked of the owner separately. The simplification pays both back. But nothing stops the next delta from adding a bullet to `## RULES` again, which is how 85 prohibition words accumulated across three files in the first place. A counted ceiling makes the owner's intent self-enforcing: adding a ban means removing another one, or deliberately raising the ceiling and recording why.

## Scope
In scope:
- One line limit of 240 for worker.md, reviewer.md and manager.md.
- A test counting the words `never`, `do not` and `don't` (case-insensitive) per file against a ceiling.
- Measure the three counts AFTER the rewrites and set each ceiling to the measured value plus 2. Record both numbers in design delta §4.6. Do not reword a role file to reach a number invented before the rewrite existed: that is the same move W4 forbids.
Out of scope:
- Any further edit to the role files' content.
- The documentation updates, which are their own bead.

## Components Touched
- test/roles-content.test.ts, docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260917b-simplify-roles.md (§4.6 numbers)

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- bm-wp-223-kve2, bm-wp-224-cw7p, bm-wp-225-utnl: all three files must be rewritten before the ceilings can be measured.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- The counter runs on the raw markdown, so an example that quotes the word `never` inside a code span also counts. That is acceptable: the ceiling is an upper bound, not an exact measure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All three files assert a 240-line limit.
- A prohibition-budget assertion exists per file, with the ceiling equal to the measured count plus 2.
- Design delta §4.6 records the measured count and the ceiling for each file.
- `npx vitest run test/roles-content.test.ts` green.

## Primary Proof
`npx vitest run test/roles-content.test.ts` read from its exit status, plus the measured counts quoted in the close reason.

## Reversibility
Revert the two assertions in the test file.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260917b-simplify-roles.md#wp-226
Requirements: PRD REQ-032(b)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260917b-simplify-roles.md §4.6
close_reason: Measured the three rewritten files and set the ceilings from the measurement, and replaced the metric itself. Measurements: worker.md 273->266 lines with the RULES block 52->30 (-42%) and 19->5 items; reviewer.md 137->135 with RULES 26->14 (-46%) and 8->4; manager.md 142->147 with RULES 27->25 and 11->5. New line limits are measured + 10: 276 / 145 / 157, replacing 280 / 240 / 240. METRIC CHANGED, and this is the part worth reading: design delta 4.6 originally proposed capping prohibition words (never / do not / don't) at 22/12/14. That is the wrong proxy and I dropped it, for two reasons. The b1 review measured the count OUTSIDE the RULES block alone at 22/8/15, so the preset ceilings were unreachable before a single limit was written. Worse, the counter matches 'do not know', 'do not relay it again' and 'do not retry in a loop' — instructions, not limits on the agent's power — so by that metric manager.md scored WORSE after the simplification (28->30), which is nonsense. What is capped instead is what the owner actually pointed at: each file must state exactly its agreed number of hard limits (5/4/5), the RULES block must fit its ceiling (34/18/29 = measured + 4), and no stray bullet may hide a sixth limit under the numbers. The 240-line target of design 4.5 is recorded as NOT MET with the reason: the transition table moves rules rather than deleting them, so the prose stays and only the RULES block shrinks; squeezing to reach a number invented before the rewrite existed is the exact move W4 forbids. Validated, read from its own exit status: npm run verify exit 0 (86 files, 1854 tests, build ok). Negative control on the new budget: adding a fifth limit to reviewer.md as a numbered item turns it red, and adding the same thing disguised as a bullet turns it red too; file restored byte-identical both times.

title: Hook sets the agent mode, so no prompt has to teach it
description:
## Objective
Make `before("agent.create")` choose `modeId` for `bm-worker` and `bm-reviewer`, so neither the Manager nor the Worker has to call `inspect_provider` or carry a mode-selection paragraph.

## Context
The owner asked for instructions that help an agent work, not a control framework it has to track. A measured 36-48% of each role file is transcription rather than judgement, and the mode recipe is the clearest case: 7 lines in `worker.md` and 7 in `manager.md` that exist only because nothing else sets the value. Verified against @getpaseo/plugin 0.8: the hook receives `AgentSessionConfig` and may return a modified copy, `modeId` is one of its fields, and `context.paseo.providers.listModes(provider)` enumerates the choices. `role-hook.ts` today uses exactly one of the eight available levers (`systemPrompt`).

## Scope
In scope:
- In the existing `bm-*` branch of the hook, resolve and set `config.modeId` when the caller left it empty: `bm-worker` gets the provider's no-approval-prompt mode, `bm-reviewer` gets an automatic mode that opens neither full access nor the network (REQ-026c).
- For `bm-reviewer` only, downgrade a caller-chosen full-access or `dangerous` mode to the safe one and log it.
- Create the phase revert copy: `plugin/roles/*.md` plus `test/roles-content.test.ts` into a `mktemp -d` directory kept until the documentation bead of this delta closes.
Out of scope:
- `bm-manager`: `manager.ensure` already sets its mode; two places deciding one value is worse than one.
- Labels: the hook input has no labels field (verified), so label rules stay in the prompts.
- Removing the mode paragraphs from the role files: that is bm-wp-229 and bm-wp-231.

## Components Touched
- plugin/server/role-hook.ts, test/plugin-role-hook.test.ts

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- none

## Assumptions / Constraints
- The hook must NEVER break agent creation. `listModes` throwing, returning nothing, or a provider with no matching mode all mean: return the request untouched.
- The existing `systemPrompt` behaviour must not change.

## Selection rule (owner decision bm-msy, 2026-09-15 — copied from the prose it replaces, not invented)
Candidates come from `context.paseo.providers.listModes(config.provider)`; each mode is `{ id, label, colorTier }` with `colorTier` one of `planning`, `safe`, `moderate`, `dangerous`.
- `bm-worker`: the first `dangerous` mode (the one that runs without approval prompts: `bypassPermissions` on Claude, `full-access` on Codex). Never `planning`. None → the first `moderate`, else the first `safe`.
- `bm-reviewer`: the mode with id `auto` when present; else the first `moderate` whose id and label mention neither "full" nor "network"; else the first `safe`. Never `dangerous`, never `planning`.
Verified read-only on the owner's daemon (2026-09-17): `listModes("bm-worker")` returned plan[planning], default[safe], acceptEdits[moderate], auto[moderate], bypassPermissions[dangerous]; `listModes("bm-reviewer")` returned auto[moderate], auto-review[moderate], full-access[dangerous]. The alias resolves to the underlying provider, so the rule picks `bypassPermissions` and `auto` there.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Mode ids differ per provider and are not guessable; everything comes from `listModes`. Do not hard-code an id.
- Once the role files stop teaching mode selection, this hook is load-bearing: a silent failure would leave a Worker in a prompting mode. Log every fallback loudly (`[paseo-bm]` prefix, like the other hooks) so the acceptance run can see it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Caller left `modeId` empty → the hook sets the role's mode.
- Caller set a mode → kept, except a full-access/dangerous mode on `bm-reviewer`, which is downgraded.
- `listModes` rejects or returns no usable mode → the request is returned unchanged and agent creation still succeeds.
- `bm-manager` creations pass through untouched.
- The phase revert copy exists with four files.

## Primary Proof
`npx vitest run test/plugin-role-hook.test.ts` with one case per acceptance criterion, then `npm run verify`, each read from its own exit status.

## Reversibility
Revert role-hook.ts and its test; the hook falls back to today's behaviour where the agent chooses.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260917c-context-engineering.md#wp-227
Requirements: PRD REQ-026(c), REQ-032(a)
Design refs: delta 20260917c §4.6, K2, K3
close_reason:
Re-closed after review b2 finding C1 (blocking) and review b3 finding B7 (blocking).

C1: the plugin host gives a before hook 30 seconds and then FAILS the agent creation, while the SDK's listModes timeout is 90 s and the daemon waits for provider warm-up — so the hook as written could break Worker, Reviewer or Manager creation on a cold daemon, the exact thing its own comment promised never to do. Fixed: every lookup and the whole preparation (extras, profile, modes, runtime facts) now run under ONE 5 second budget (LOOKUP_TIMEOUT_MS, well under the host's 30 s); on timeout the agent is still created with its role instructions and no mode, and one line is logged. withTimeout returns a SENTINEL (TIMED_OUT), not null, because a lookup may legitimately answer null — the first version of this fix conflated the two and would have logged a timeout for a real empty answer. listModes is also called with the agent's cwd so the daemon can answer from the snapshot it already warmed.

B7: the bm-msy rule has two halves — "the profile's mode if it has one; otherwise <the chain>" — and only the chain had survived. profileModeOf reads config.get().config.agentProfiles the same way manager.ensure reads the Manager's profile; chooseModeId now takes profileModeId and prefers it for the Worker, and for the Reviewer prefers it unless it is dangerous or planning. runtimeFactsOf prefers the profile mode too, and passes it even when listModes failed, because Paseo validates the value and reports its own error. The Reviewer's full/network name filter now also reads the mode's description (review b2, non-blocking).

Validated, read from its own exit status: npx vitest run test/plugin-role-hook.test.ts test/plugin-role-runtime-facts.test.ts = 55 passed; npm run verify exit 0 (87 files, 1924 tests, build ok).

One assertion changed, recorded: 'listModes called with bm-worker' now asserts the first call is ['bm-worker', { cwd }], because passing the cwd hint is part of the C1 fix.

Negative control, 5 mutations, each red and restored byte-identical: the Worker ignoring its profile mode; the Reviewer accepting a dangerous profile mode; the hook awaiting the preparation without a timeout; dropping the cwd hint; and withTimeout resolving null instead of the sentinel.
