title: BM-REPORT drops the guardrail line, consumers follow
description:
## Objective
Remove the self-reported `guardrail` counter from the `BM-REPORT` contract and make every consumer use the count the plugin derives.

## Context
Once the plugin counts (bm-wp-228 counter bead), the Worker's `guardrail: batch <id> reviews n/max; total n/budget; userAllowedExtra n` line is a second, less reliable source for the same number. Keeping both invites the Dashboard to show a wrong figure next to a right one. Owner decision Q17.

## Scope
In scope:
- `plugin/shared/contracts.ts`: `guardrailReportSchema` and the `guardrail` field stay but become optional/nullable so stored traces still parse; nothing requires them.
- `plugin/server/bm-report.ts` AND `plugin/shared/bm-report.ts` (the two must stay identical except the import line): stop treating `guardrail` as expected; an old report that still carries it must parse exactly as before.
- `plugin/server/traces.ts`, `plugin/server/workflow-steps.ts` and the client model: use the derived `reviewCalls` as the primary number.
Out of scope:
- Editing `worker.md` and `manager.md` to drop the line: those are their own beads.
- Recomputing historical traces.

## Components Touched
- plugin/shared/contracts.ts, plugin/server/bm-report.ts, plugin/shared/bm-report.ts, plugin/server/traces.ts, plugin/server/workflow-steps.ts, the client model, and their tests

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- The counter bead: the derived number must exist before anything relies on it.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Backward compatibility is not optional: a stored trace written today must still open.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A report WITHOUT a guardrail line parses with no error and no missing-field warning.
- A stored report WITH one still parses, and its values are still readable.
- The Dashboard shows the derived count as the primary figure.
- `npm run verify` exits 0.

## Primary Proof
A round-trip test over both report shapes plus the existing trace-store tests, read from the exit status.

## Reversibility
Revert the contract and parser changes; the field returns to required.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260917c-context-engineering.md#wp-228
Requirements: PRD REQ-037 (errata), REQ-034
Design refs: delta 20260917c §4.7, §5
close_reason: Merged into bm-wp-228-x3ej during the polishing-beads pass, no work done under this id. Reading the code showed this bead had almost nothing of its own: parseGuardrail(undefined) already returns null and guardrail is not an incompleteFields entry, so a report without the line already parses cleanly; plugin/client/dashboard-model.ts already shows the derived reviewCalls as the primary figure and uses guardrailReported only for the mismatch note; and plugin/server/workflow-steps.ts must keep its guardrail.polish branch for old traces. What remained was three compatibility tests, which belong with the bead that makes the self-reported counter unnecessary. Its dependents (bm-wp-229-nt2t, bm-wp-231-qkxb) now depend on bm-wp-228-x3ej directly.

title: Plugin counts the review budget and tells the Manager
description:
## Objective
Move the review-call counter from the Worker's head into the plugin, have the plugin tell the Manager once when a request goes over its tier budget, and prove the `BM-REPORT` contract works without the Worker's self-reported `guardrail` line.

## Context
The 2026-09-17 acceptance run proved the split: the Dashboard counted 4 review calls correctly while the Worker self-reported 5. The count already exists in the trace store (`reviewRequests` with `batchId`, `reviewCalls`). Asking two agents to track a number the system already knows costs prompt space in both files and is wrong often enough to matter. Owner decision Q17: the system counts, agents stop counting. REQ-037 stays a behavioural guardrail — the plugin reports, the Manager decides, the user permits.

## Scope
In scope:
- After the collector has written the record of ANY agent of the request — Worker, Reviewer or Manager — recompute the review calls of that `requestId` and compare with the tier budget (Small 1, Medium 4, Large 6). The tier comes from the latest `BM-REPORT` of the request. The Manager's own turn end matters: the Worker's last report usually wakes the Manager, so a notice deferred at the Worker's turn end can only go out when the Manager's turn ends (review b1, B2).
- Over budget → `paseo.agents.ref(managerId).send(...)` ONCE per request, with exactly this text (design delta §4.7, owner decision Q21 — the Manager asks the user, it does not cancel on its own):

```
BM-BUDGET requestId: <requestId>
The Worker has used <n> review calls; the <tier> budget is <max>. Ask the user whether to continue or to cancel the Worker's run, and wait for the answer. Do not cancel on your own: the user may already have allowed the extra calls in the Worker's chat.
```
 The Manager is the Worker's parent: `event.agent.parentAgentId` (collector.ts already reads it the same way).
- Count with what already exists, do not re-parse timelines: `reviewCallsOf(reviewerIds, records)` in `plugin/server/traces.ts` over the request's reconstructed trace; the Dashboard's figure and the notice must be the same number.
- Contract compatibility (absorbed from bm-wp-228-nszk): tests that a `BM-REPORT` WITHOUT a `guardrail:` line parses with `guardrail: null`, no `incompleteFields` entry and no unparsed field; that a stored report WITH one still parses to the same values; and that a trace summary with `guardrailReported: null` renders the derived count with no "review counts disagree" note.
- `PaseoAgentHandle.send()` REPLACES the current turn of a running agent — that is how `stop-propagation.ts` interrupts a Reviewer. So refresh the Manager first and only send when it is not `running`; otherwise defer to a later `turn_ended`.
Out of scope:
- Blocking anything: the plugin reports, it never stops the Worker.
- `userAllowedExtra`: it disappears entirely, because the Manager relayed the user's permission and therefore already knows.
- Removing the `guardrail:` line from worker.md and the supervision paragraph from manager.md: those are the two role-file beads.

## Components Touched
- a new module under plugin/server/, wired in plugin/index.server.ts next to registerStopPropagation, plus its test
- tests only for plugin/server/bm-report.ts and plugin/client/dashboard-model.ts; no code change there: `parseGuardrail(undefined)` already returns null, `guardrail` is not an `incompleteFields` entry, and `dashboard-model.ts` already shows `reviewCalls` as the primary figure and uses `guardrailReported` only for the mismatch note
- NOT plugin/server/workflow-steps.ts: its `guardrail.polish` branch is the exact negative for traces written before the workflow-skills delta and must stay

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- none

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Follow the shape of `stop-propagation.ts`: page `agents.list`, filter again locally, never trust the filter, refresh before acting.
- One notice per `requestId`, remembered in memory for the process lifetime.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Interrupting a Manager mid-answer would be worse than the miscount it fixes. The not-running check is the whole safety of this bead.
- Handler order: the collector records the Worker's turn in its own `agent.turn_ended` handler. Counting before that record is written sees the previous total. Read after the collector has persisted (call from the collector's path, or read the store after it), and cover the ordering in a test.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Counts correctly on a sample timeline carrying a first review and a re-review.
- Sends exactly one notice when over budget, and none while inside it.
- Does not send while the Manager is `running`; sends at a later turn end instead — including the Manager's own turn end, in the sequence "Worker's report wakes the Manager, Worker's turn ends (deferred), Manager's turn ends (sent)".
- The notice text is exactly the one above.
- Any failure while reading the trace, refreshing the Manager or sending the notice is logged and swallowed; it never breaks the collector or the Worker's turn handling.
- The three contract-compatibility tests above pass.

## Primary Proof
Unit tests over a constructed timeline plus a fake Paseo api that records sends, read from the exit status, then `npm run verify`.

## Reversibility
Remove the module and its wiring; nothing else depends on it until the next bead.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260917c-context-engineering.md#wp-228
Requirements: PRD REQ-037 (errata), REQ-034
Design refs: delta 20260917c §4.7, §5, K5
close_reason:
Re-closed after review b2, which found five blocking defects in this module plus one worthless test.

C2 — a self-feeding notice storm: a Manager turn end checked every request that Manager had ever handled and `told` lives only in memory, so after any reload the next Manager turn end would announce old finished requests, and each notice starts a Manager turn whose end announces the next. Fixed: only a Worker's or Reviewer's turn end DISCOVERS an overrun (and records it in a new `pending` map); a Manager turn end can only FLUSH what is pending for that Manager in this process.
C3 — two turn ends of one request both sent, because `told` was written after the awaited refresh/send. Fixed: the request is claimed before the first await, and the claim is released in a finally block when the notice did not go out.
C4 — the SDK always attaches a messageId to send(), the daemon stores it as clientMessageId, and the collector reads exactly that field to tell the user's words from an agent's: the notice was recorded as a USER message, shown as "you" on the Metric screen, counted among user messages, and could become a request's text. Fixed with a new plugin/server/notices.ts holding BUDGET_NOTICE_MARKER and REVIEWER_STOP_NOTICE_PREFIX plus isPluginNotice(); collector.ts and live-timeline.ts now classify such a message as origin "agent", traces.ts skips it in firstUserText, and reviewCallsOf uses the shared predicate instead of its own copy of the stop prefix. The stop notice had the same defect and is fixed by the same change.
C5 — send() un-archives an archived agent and starts a turn on it, which breaks ADR-005. Fixed: an archived or closed Manager is left alone, the pending entry is dropped and one line is logged.
C6 — the multi-request test seeded one request and proved nothing. Replaced by a test with two over-budget requests, one of them yesterday's finished one, that asserts a fresh process stays silent at a Manager turn end, that only the request found by a Reviewer turn end is flushed, and that the old request is never named.

Validated, read from its own exit status: npm run verify exit 0 (87 files, 1930 tests, build ok).

Negative control, 5 mutations, each red and restored byte-identical: letting the Manager discover overruns itself; claiming the request after the await; waking an archived Manager; counting a notice as the user's message; letting a notice become the request text.

Design delta §4.7 now records all four rules so the next change cannot undo them by accident.

title: worker.md: one loop, beads as the instrument, two worked examples
description:
## Objective
Rewrite `plugin/roles/worker.md` so an agent reads one decision loop instead of cross-referencing seven schedules, sees what a good bead and a good question set actually look like, and understands that its job is the user's change while beads are the instrument that keeps that work split, ordered and provable.

## Context
Owner, 2026-09-17: instructions must help the AI do the job, not be a control framework so dense it causes confusion; and "bộ agent này ... không phải chỉ dành cho 1 Beads, nó có thể làm nhiều loại việc khác nhau, Beads chỉ là cơ chế để kiểm soát công việc tốt hơn". Read as a Worker, today's file gives its first actionable instruction at line ~42 after 32 lines of limits, hands over a ten-field bead contract without ever showing a good bead, and makes the implement loop carry six simultaneous constraints. It also frames bead maintenance as the goal, which is why an agent optimises for the tool instead of the outcome.

## Scope
In scope, following design delta §4.2, §4.3 and §4.8:
- Opening states the outcome the Worker owes the user, and that beads are the instrument, not the goal.
- `## RULES` keeps the five limits, tightened.
- ONE section "what you do next": the whole job as a single ordered loop with the tier branches inline, absorbing today's Step 1 to Step 4 and the report moments.
- Reference blocks the loop points at: sizing, splitting the work, proving a change, asking, reviewing, reporting, being stopped.
- The twelve stop-and-ask triggers collapse into a principle with TWO halves (design delta §4.3): (1) ask when the answer would change what you build and you cannot get it from the artifacts — naming the REQ-026(d) cases outright: editing a frozen document, widening the scope, deleting or merging existing beads; (2) ask when you are stuck: an attempt gave no new evidence, an error repeats, or a change cannot be checked. Use exactly these three examples: changing behaviour existing users rely on (a generic login error that breaks a QA script matching the old string) → ask; a requirement beyond the user's words (adding a password-attempt limit because it seems missing) → do not do it, record it as a suggestion, or ask if it blocks you; stuck (the same build error a third time after three different fixes) → stop and ask, listing the three attempts.
- Keep the precedence as one positive sentence in the opening: skills say HOW; on safety, budget, reporting, when to ask and scope this file decides (skills the Worker loads really do conflict — implementing-beads suggests per-bead review and parallel sub-agents).
- A WORKED BEAD EXAMPLE, drawn from a real bead of this repo's graph and trimmed, annotated with what each part buys (Primary Proof and Reversibility are there because they are what makes a piece of work prove and revert on its own).
- A WORKED QUESTION SET showing the shape, replacing the count-and-format rules.
- Non-software work is first class: proving a change means the cheapest evidence the outcome happened — a conclusion with sources for research, a readable state for configuration, a check for code.
- The Reviewer brief the Worker sends now carries the stage criteria (paths in the workflow skills), because a Reviewer handles one stage only.
- The Reviewer mode-selection paragraph disappears: the hook downgrades the `full-access` a Reviewer would otherwise inherit from a no-prompt Worker (design delta K10). The `guardrail:` line disappears and the Worker stops counting the request's total review calls (owner decisions Q17, Q21): the plugin counts and the Manager asks the user. The per-BATCH rule stays: one first review and one re-review; blocking findings left after the re-review → stop and ask.
Out of scope:
- Any change to the tiers, the 1/4/6 budget, the three asking moments, the five required skills, the leaf-bead contract's content, or the rest of the `BM-REPORT` block.
- reviewer.md and manager.md.

## Components Touched
- plugin/roles/worker.md, plugin/server/worker-instructions.ts (regenerated), test/roles-content.test.ts

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- The hook bead bm-wp-227-lz81 (the mode paragraph can only go once the hook sets the mode).
- The counter bead bm-wp-228-x3ej (the `guardrail` line can only go once the plugin owns the count).

## Assumptions / Constraints
- English (repo language rule); the Vietnamese section names in the design are descriptions, not text to copy.
- `## RULES` stays the first heading with exactly five limits.
- The file MAY get longer: owner decision Q16 measures the ratio of judgement to compliance, not the line count.
- Run `npm run generate:role-instructions` before closing.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Reframing beads as an instrument could loosen bead discipline, which the owner complained about earlier ("bead ít quá"). The worked example and the split rule stay, and the acceptance run measures leaf count against a floor of 12.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Exactly one "what you do next" section, holding the whole loop with tier branches inline.
- The opening says beads are the instrument and names the user's outcome as the job.
- A worked bead example and a worked question set are present, and are examples, not lists.
- Non-code evidence is named explicitly in the proving section.
- No Reviewer mode-selection paragraph, no `guardrail` line, no total-budget self-count; the per-batch rule is still there.
- The two-half asking principle, the REQ-026(d) cases and the three decided examples are present.
- Every rule of the old file is either in the new one or recorded as deliberately dropped in the close reason.
- roles-content and plugin-bundle-cjs tests green.

## Primary Proof
A section-by-section walk of design delta §4.3 recorded in the close reason, plus `npx vitest run test/roles-content.test.ts test/plugin-bundle-cjs.test.ts` read from its exit status.

## Reversibility
Copy worker.md back from the phase copy and re-run the generator.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260917c-context-engineering.md#wp-229
Requirements: PRD REQ-032(a)(b), REQ-036, REQ-022
Design refs: delta 20260917c §4.2, §4.3, §4.8
close_reason:
Re-closed after review b3, which found five blocking defects in this file.

B1 — the loop never said which STAGE value each batch uses, and the old "b1 (documents, plan included)" and "the plan inside documents (Large)" notes were gone, so a Large b1 brief could go out as `documents` with no plan criteria and a Medium b1 as `documents` with no beads read. Every branch of the loop now names its stage (Small: one review, stage implementation; Medium b1 = plan with the sections and beads together, b2 = implementation; Large b1 = documents with the plan in it, b2 = beads, b3 = implementation), and the documents row of the brief table says a Large b1 must add the plan row's criteria.

B2 — the tier table gives a Small request one call in all while Reviewing promised every batch a re-review, and Q21 had removed the rule that used to settle it. REQ-037(e) decides it, so no owner call was needed: a Small request has exactly one review; a blocking finding there is fixed and then reported with `blocked`, never re-reviewed.

B3 — the worked question set said "I will take (a) unless you say otherwise", teaching exactly the behaviour RULE 5 forbids and the first live run showed (the Worker proceeded on a default nobody answered). Each option now states its own cost, the recommendation is marked, the example ends with "I am waiting for your answers before I start", and the prose says silence is not an answer.

B4 and B5 — the example bead was paseo-bm's own control mechanism, introduced as "this repository's own graph", which is false for a Worker in the user's repository and is the self-referential prompt text the delta set out to remove; it also lacked Dependencies-era fields' companions, the checklist's Validation / Definition of Done and a Provenance naming the request. Replaced by a REAL bead from ordinary user work — the 15-minute lockout after five failed logins, from the acceptance run's own graph in the demo repository — trimmed and translated, now showing all ten parts including Validation / Definition of Done and a Provenance whose first line is `Request: req-… — "…"`.

B6 — "The plugin gives it a mode that cannot write or reach the network" is false: the Paseo bundle describes Codex `auto` as "Edit files and run commands". Now simply "The plugin sets the Reviewer's mode, so you do not choose one."

Also, non-blocking from the same review: the close reason is `<the evidence: a command and its result, or what you read back>` instead of `<command and result>`, so non-code work fits.

Measured: 361 -> 382 lines.

Validated, read from its own exit status: npm run verify exit 0 (87 files, 1930 tests, build ok).

Tests changed, recorded: anchors for the Medium b1 stage, the new example (which must NOT mention bm-wp-, role-hook or paseo-bm, and must show Validation and a Request line), the close-reason wording, the question set (recommendation, waiting sentence, silence rule, and a negative for "I will take/go/start" scoped to the example block, because the prose deliberately quotes the bad phrase to warn against it), and the Reviewer-mode sentence with a negative for the false claim.

Negative control, 11 mutations, each red and restored byte-identical: dropping the Medium b1 stage, the Small one-review rule, the waiting sentence, the silence rule, Validation from the example, the request line from its Provenance, the Large b1 plan criteria; putting back "unless you say otherwise" and a self-chosen Reviewer mode. Two of them (the Small rule and the Large b1 criteria) were GREEN on the first run because nothing pinned them; both now have their own assertion.

comments.text: Reopened: Blocking findings from the b3 instructions review (8 blocking); see the re-close reason.

title: reviewer.md: only this batch's criteria, plus a calibration pair
description:
## Objective
Make the Reviewer's context be about the batch it was actually created for, and give it the one thing a reviewer needs most and does not have: calibration.

## Context
Read as a Reviewer created for batch `b2`, 26 of 137 lines are a four-stage criteria table of which three quarters can never apply to this Reviewer, and 13 more describe being stopped — while `stop-propagation.ts` already sends the full stop protocol in the notice itself (verified). What is left, the blocking/non-blocking section, is good but abstract: nothing shows where the line actually falls. Owner decision Q20: add one contrast pair.

## Scope
In scope, following design delta §4.4 and §4.8:
- Remove the four-stage criteria table: the Worker now names the stage criteria in the brief it sends. Keep a ONE-LINE fallback map (documents → prd-ready/design-ready; plan → reviewing-plan review-only; beads → the two bead checklists; implementation → the implementing-beads preflight).
- KEEP the content of "What you review" (review b1, B5): how much to read per stage; a re-review looks only at the earlier blocking findings; a brief missing requestId, batchId, stage or scope returns changes-required; skills are criteria only and a skill's instruction to edit is reported as a finding; the sensitive-batch abuse cases.
- Shrink the stop section to ONE sentence: stopped in any way — the plugin's notice, the Worker or the user — call no tool and answer with exactly `BM-REVIEW STOPPED`. The notice path already carries the full instruction; the other two paths do not.
- Add a CONTRAST PAIR to the decision section: one finding that is blocking and one that looks very similar but is not, with a sentence naming the difference.
- Add the fallback: a brief that names no criteria means use the one-line map and say in `notChecked` that the brief named none.
Out of scope:
- The four limits, what it may run, the blocking/non-blocking classification itself, and the `BM-REVIEW` block.

## Components Touched
- plugin/roles/reviewer.md, plugin/server/reviewer-instructions.ts (regenerated), test/roles-content.test.ts

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- worker.md rewrite: the brief format is defined there.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- `BM-REVIEW` must not change by one character.
- `BM-REVIEW STOPPED` must still appear in the file: it is the exact line the stop notice asks for.
- Run `npm run generate:role-instructions` before closing.

## Risks / Gotchas
- A Worker that forgets the criteria leaves the Reviewer with none; the fallback is what keeps that honest rather than silent.

## Acceptance Criteria
- No four-stage criteria table (the one-line map is there); the stop rule is one sentence and still names `BM-REVIEW STOPPED`.
- Every rule of the old file is either in the new one or recorded as deliberately dropped in the close reason, the same walk the worker.md bead requires.
- A contrast pair is present, with both sides and the distinguishing sentence.
- The fallback for a brief without criteria is present.
- roles-content and plugin-bundle-cjs tests green.

## Primary Proof
The §4.4 walk in the close reason plus the two test files read from the exit status.

## Reversibility
Copy reviewer.md back from the phase copy and re-run the generator.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260917c-context-engineering.md#wp-230
Requirements: PRD REQ-032(a)(b), REQ-024(e)
Design refs: delta 20260917c §4.4, §4.8, K6
close_reason:
Re-closed after review b3's two non-blocking findings against this file, both fixed because each was a gap rather than a matter of style.

The one-line fallback map named one checklist per stage while design §4.4 specifies two for `plan` and two for `beads`; it now lists plan-ready-for-beads.md beside reviewing-plan, and readiness-checklist.md beside the leaf checklist. The `implementation` stage talked only about a code diff and tests, so work that is not code had nowhere to land; it now says the whole change, and adds: when the outcome is not code, check the evidence the bead named — a conclusion against its sources, a configuration read back, a screen or endpoint against the captured response.

title: manager.md: four actions, and the user-facing part it never had
description:
## Objective
Cut the Manager down to the four actions it performs, and grow the one part of its job the file barely covers: being useful to the user.

## Context
Read as a Manager, the job is restate, delegate, confirm, track — four actions — yet 60 of 150 lines are needed to perform the third, half of them a `create_agent` recipe. Meanwhile the Manager is the user's only point of contact and everything about talking to them fits in seven lines at the end. The mode half of the recipe goes to the hook, and the budget table and supervision paragraph go to the plugin's notice.

## Scope
In scope, following design delta §4.5:
- A "what you do next" section with the four actions.
- The Worker-creation recipe compressed. The mode-selection RULE goes, but the Manager STILL passes a mode (design delta K10: the daemon refuses a Worker without one before any hook runs, because the installed Manager is not in a no-prompt mode). One sentence: pass `settings.modeId` exactly as the `## Runtime facts` line at the end of these instructions says; if creation fails, report Paseo's message word for word, as for any creation failure. No `inspect_provider`.
- The budget table and the supervision paragraph replaced by the handling of the plugin's `BM-BUDGET` notice (owner decision Q21): show the user the numbers, ask whether to continue or cancel, and wait. Never cancel on the notice alone — the user may have allowed the calls in the Worker's chat.
- "Talking to the user" grown to cover what the Manager actually owes them: what it says at each Worker phase, what it does while waiting, how it presents questions and suggestions.
Out of scope:
- The five limits, the skills check (including telling the user about a missing required skill on `finished`, without cancelling), the `Continue <requestId>.` resume line, the label and provider names, follow-ups going to the existing Worker, creation failures reported with their cause and no retry loop, the stop-a-Worker and archive/delete handling.

## Components Touched
- plugin/roles/manager.md, plugin/server/manager-instructions.ts (regenerated), test/roles-content.test.ts

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- The hook bead bm-wp-227-lz81 and the counter bead bm-wp-228-x3ej.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- English; `## RULES` first with exactly five limits.
- Run `npm run generate:role-instructions` before closing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- One "what you do next" section naming the four actions.
- No mode-selection rule and no `inspect_provider`; exactly one sentence pointing at the Runtime facts line; no budget table, no self-counting supervision.
- The `BM-BUDGET` handling says ask the user and wait.
- Every rule of the old file is either in the new one or recorded as deliberately dropped in the close reason.
- The plugin-notice sentence is present and says the Manager still decides.
- The user-facing section covers each Worker phase.
- roles-content and plugin-bundle-cjs tests green.

## Primary Proof
The §4.5 walk in the close reason plus the two test files read from the exit status.

## Reversibility
Copy manager.md back from the phase copy and re-run the generator.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260917c-context-engineering.md#wp-231
Requirements: PRD REQ-032(a)(b), REQ-020(d), REQ-037

beside the Worker's BM-REPORT and the status tools: without it the limit
forbade acting on BM-BUDGET, which the same file mandates.

due until it asks or finishes") -- the report the Manager receives most often

case. Negative controls (delete the sentence, run the suite): received bullet

RED.

description:

## Context

title: Acceptance run: measure the new instructions against the two earlier runs
description:
## Objective
Find out whether the rewritten instructions actually make the agents faster and sharper, by running the same request a third time and comparing.

## Context
Owner decision Q18. Two runs of "build a user management system and a login screen for Team Portal" already exist: 2026-09-16 (27 minutes, $12.88, 8 beads, 1 skill, 0 question rounds) and 2026-09-17 (41.4 minutes, $20.18, 12 beads, 5 skills, 3 question rounds). The second bought quality with time and money. Nobody knows how much of that cost was the work and how much was instruction overhead; this run is the only way to find out. Without it the whole delta rests on argument.

## Scope
In scope:
- Ask the owner for permission, back up `~/.paseo/config.json`, check no `bm-*` agent is running, install the payload.
- Run the same request through Beads Manager, answering as the user with the standard answers.
- Run the Manager in its INSTALLED DEFAULT mode, not the no-prompt mode earlier runs used: those runs could never hit design delta K10, where the daemon refuses a Worker created without an explicit mode. The Worker must be created on the first try from the Runtime facts line.
- Collect: wall time, time to first bead, total estimated cost (priced part and unpriced tokens separately), Manager turns, question rounds, leaf beads (for reference only), bead readiness (every leaf has one outcome, Primary Proof and Reversibility; polishing split at most once), review calls, skills used, the blocking findings an independent unsandboxed review finds afterwards, the mode of every Reviewer, and whether any agent did the opposite of a sentence in its role file.
- Write the record comparing all three runs against the target table in design delta §6, and state plainly whether the delta passed.
Out of scope:
- Archiving or deleting any agent: the owner's action.
- Fixing anything the run exposes: that is a new bead.

## Components Touched
- docs/operations/ (new run record), the owner's daemon (install), ~/bm-demo working copies

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- The documentation bead: everything must be recorded before the payload goes on a live daemon.
- Record the phase revert copy's path (in /tmp/bm-phase-copy-20260917c.txt) in the run record, so the closing bead can use it if something must be restored.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Ask before installing. Restore the config if anything goes wrong. Never run `paseo daemon restart` or `stop`.
- The decoy `.env` in the sample repo must not be read.

## Risks / Gotchas
- The measure that matters most for the reframing is bead READINESS, not bead count: `worker.md` itself says the number of beads is never evidence. If readiness drops, the reframing loosened bead discipline and part of this delta has to be given back.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The record carries every metric of design delta §6 for the new run, beside the two earlier ones, plus the three pass/fail checks (default-mode Manager creates a Worker; every Reviewer in auto; no instruction acted against).
- A verdict: passed, or a named list of what must be restored.
- No agent archived or deleted; config sha256 unchanged at the end.

## Primary Proof
The run record with timeline evidence and the Dashboard numbers, plus the independent review's findings.

## Reversibility
Reinstall the previous payload; the run itself changes nothing in this repository.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260917c-context-engineering.md#wp-233
Requirements: PRD REQ-032, REQ-036, REQ-037
Design refs: delta 20260917c §6

title: Trace store keeps turns whose turn id Paseo reused
description:
## Objective
The trace reader keeps every distinct turn of an agent even when Paseo reuses a turn id, while still dropping a true duplicate written twice after a plugin reload.

## Steps to Reproduce
In the owner's store (wks_a217b1fc9568ab78), Manager d6fc9b1c has foreground-turn-1, -2 and -3 twice each, first messages at 04:19-04:22 and again at 04:27-04:31 on 2026-09-17; Worker 9ddf32c5 has foreground-turn-1 twice (04:19 and 04:27). readRecords keeps only the later record of each pair, so the Manager's opening turn (the owner's MR question) and the Worker's first turn (12,476 output tokens) disappear from the Metric screen.

## Context
plugin/server/trace-store.ts dedupeRecords keys on (agentId, turnId) and keeps the latest at, exactly as dashboard design §3.3 says, because the collector can write the same turn twice after a reload. The design assumed turn ids are unique per agent; Paseo renumbers them (design delta 20260917d §5).

## Scope
In scope:
- Key = (agentId, turnId, fingerprint of the turn's messages): a digest over the text of `sent` then `received`, in order. A record with no messages keeps the old key (agentId, turnId).
- The time-based key this bead first prescribed was CHECKED and REJECTED on 2026-09-17: collector.ts stamps messages with the write time whenever the refetch fails (delta 20260917d section 4 B). Owner chose the content fingerprint the same day. Do not reintroduce a time component.
- The same key in the reassignment merge path if it uses its own dedupe (dashboard design §3.5 step 4).
Out of scope:
- The cross-Manager folding problem (the other bead of this delta).

## Components Touched
- plugin/server/trace-store.ts, possibly the reassignment merge, test/plugin-trace-store.test.ts

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- none

## Assumptions / Constraints
- A reload rewrite has the same timeline items as the first write; this is the assumption the scope tells you to confirm in collector.ts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Same agent and turn id, different turn content (04:19 and 04:27) → both kept.
- Same agent, turn id and content, different record `at` → one kept (the later).
- Same content but every message time different (the write-time fallback) → still one kept.
- A record with no messages → deduped by (agentId, turnId) as before.
- The existing trace-store tests (including test/plugin-trace-store.test.ts:238-252) stay green.
- npm run verify exits 0.

## Primary Proof
The three new cases plus the existing store tests, read from the exit status; negative control: dropping the fingerprint from the key turns the reused-id case red.

## Reversibility
Revert dedupeRecords and its tests; the reader returns to (agentId, turnId).

## Provenance
Source: docs/design/paseo-bm-dashboard-delta-20260917d-request-attribution.md#4
Requirements: PRD Dashboard REQ-041, REQ-057
Design refs: dashboard design §3.3 and §4 step 2; delta 20260917d §3–§7
close_reason:
dedupeRecords now keys on (agentId, turnId, turn fingerprint).

The scope check first: I read timestampsForTurn and buildRecord and the
prescribed time key was UNSAFE -- collector.ts stamps every message with
endedAt = now() whenever the refetch fails, so a rewrite after a reload would
have got a new key and been counted twice. Bead was blocked and reported; owner
chose the content fingerprint on 2026-09-17. Delta 20260917d section 4 B, 5, 7
rewritten to record the rejected key, the evidence and the accepted residual
risk (a fallback rewrite may leave one extra row instead of losing a turn).

plugin/server/trace-store.ts: turnFingerprint() hashes the text of `sent` then
`received`, length-prefixed so "ab"+"c" cannot collide with "a"+"bc"; a record
with no messages keeps the old (agentId, turnId) key. reassignWorkspace merges
through the same dedupeRecords, so both paths are covered by one change.

Tests (test/plugin-trace-store.test.ts), five new cases: reused turn id with
different content -> both kept; one turn written twice -> later kept; a rewrite
whose every message time is the write time -> still one kept (the exact risk
that killed the time key); no messages -> old key; the re-split collision.

Negative controls: drop the fingerprint from the key -> 2 red; drop the length
prefix -> 1 red.

Docs: dashboard design section 3.3, 3.5 step 4, 6 step 2 and the test table got
errata pointing at the delta, plus a revision row; AGENTS.md gained both
verified facts (turn ids are reused; a stored message time can be the write
time).

While fixing this I also caught a literal NUL byte I had put in
plugin/server/trace-store.ts (a \u0000 separator that landed as a raw byte and
made grep treat the file as binary) -- removed, the length prefix makes a
separator unnecessary.

npm run verify: 87 files, 1941 tests passed. br lint -s all and br dep cycles
clean.

comments.author: hieunguyentrung
comments.text:
BLOCKED by its own scope check: the prescribed key is unsafe. Evidence read today.

plugin/server/collector.ts buildRecord:
  line 350  const endedAt = now().toISOString();          <- WRITE TIME
  line 367  at: typeof entry.timestamp === "string" ? entry.timestamp : endedAt
  line 369  : sliceLastTurn(items).map((item) => ({ item, at: endedAt }))

A message's `at` comes from the timeline only when timestampsForTurn's refetch
succeeds AND the entry carries a timestamp. When the refetch throws or returns
nothing (lines 246-248 swallow the error; an archived or busy agent is the
obvious case) every message of that record is stamped with the write time. A
rewrite after a plugin reload then produces a DIFFERENT first-message time for
the same turn, gets a different key, and the Dashboard counts that turn -- and
its tokens -- twice. That is the failure the scope told me to stop for.

No stable time exists in the record: `at` and `endedAt` are both now(), and
`startedAt` comes from an in-memory mark (line 420) that a reload clears.

What IS stable across a rewrite is the message TEXT: the refetch path and the
fallback carry the same timeline items. `messageId` would be better still
(protocol agent-types.d.ts: user_message has an optional messageId) but
traceMessageSchema does not store it -- adding it is a stored-schema change.

Recommended amendment to delta 20260917d section 4 B: key on
(agentId, turnId, digest of the turn's message texts), falling back to
(agentId, turnId) when the record has no messages. It distinguishes the owner's
real case (04:19 vs 04:27, different text) and survives a rewrite.
Owner's call needed: this changes the fix the Accepted delta prescribes.

title: Metric folds a Manager turn only into a request the same Manager names
description:
## Objective
A Manager turn that names no request is attached only to a request that the SAME Manager names later, so a request row never shows another Manager's text, time or tokens.

## Steps to Reproduce
Workspace with an archived Manager A whose last turn carries user text and no requestId, and a new Manager B that opens req-X eighteen hours later. traces.list shows the req-X row with A's text ("Hãy thực hiện commit, push…") and A's requestedAt (the day before); the day's request bar reads 0. Observed on the owner's workspace wks_a217b1fc9568ab78 on 2026-09-17.

## Context
Dashboard design §4 step 2 says an unnamed Manager turn belongs to the request "the Manager names in its next turn" — one Manager. plugin/server/traces.ts openBuckets pass 2 builds nextNamed and openedAfter over the Manager records of the WHOLE workspace, so the rule crosses Managers and any time gap, and fold then keeps the earliest user message as the request. The rule exists for WP-214 defect 9 (a Worker's status update arrives as a user message); that reason only holds inside one Manager's conversation.

## Scope
In scope:
- Compute nextNamed and openedAfter per Manager agent id, over that agent's own records only.
- An unnamed turn with no later request from the same Manager keeps today's behaviour: a provisional row when it has user text, nothing otherwise.
Out of scope:
- Any time-gap threshold (no evidence for one; design delta 20260917d §4).
- The duplicate-turn problem (the other bead of this delta).
- Agents without bm.role labels (recorded in the delta §6).

## Components Touched
- plugin/server/traces.ts (openBuckets pass 2), test/plugin-traces-reconstruct.test.ts

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- none

## Assumptions / Constraints
- plugin/server/review-budget.ts reconstructs traces with the same function; its tests must stay green.
- Do not start before the running code review of delta 20260917c has finished reading traces.ts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Manager A's unnamed turn plus Manager B's req-X a day later → two rows: A's provisional row with A's text, and req-X with B's text and B's requestedAt.
- Every existing pass-2 test (Worker status update, user follow-up, WP-214 F-4 request opened by a message) stays green.
- npm run verify exits 0.

## Primary Proof
The new two-Manager test plus the existing reconstruct tests, read from the exit status; negative control: removing the per-agent scoping turns the new test red.

## Reversibility

title: Stopping a Worker with Paseo's stop does not stop its running Reviewer (REQ-026f)
description:
## Objective
When the user stops a Beads Worker with Paseo's normal stop (app Stop button or paseo stop), every Reviewer that Worker is running stops too, and no child agent keeps running.

## Context
Orchestration acceptance run 4, fixture F-8a (2026-09-15): the runner ran paseo stop on Worker b47f8335 at 14:14:57Z while its Reviewer 528af102 was running. Paseo only interrupted the Worker's turn, so the Worker had no turn to follow its Stop and propagate rule. The Reviewer was not cancelled; it finished its review on its own ~60 s later, and its finish notification woke the Worker again (the Worker then asked the user instead of continuing). Nothing was running at stop + 120 s only because the review was short. REQ-026(f) requires stopping a Worker to stop its Reviewers with no orphan agents. The role-instruction path (F-8b, a stop message) is separate.

## Scope
- Investigate what Paseo 0.8 offers a plugin when an agent is stopped/interrupted (server lifecycle hooks such as before/after agent stop or cancel, agent status events) and whether a plugin may cancel another agent.
- If supported: the paseo-bm plugin cancels running agents labelled bm.role=reviewer whose paseo.parent-agent-id is the stopped Worker; unit tests with a fake server context.
- If not supported: record the limitation in the design (errata) and README troubleshooting, and escalate as a design gap to the owner; do not invent an API.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Install paseo-bm, open Beads Manager, send a Medium request.
2. While a bm-reviewer agent created by the Worker is running, stop the Worker in Paseo.
3. Result: the Reviewer keeps running until its review ends and then wakes the Worker; expected: the Reviewer stops with the Worker.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Either the plugin stops the Worker's running Reviewers when the Worker is stopped, proven by tests and a live re-run of F-8a; or a verified statement that Paseo 0.8 offers no such hook, recorded as design errata and escalated.
- npm run build, typecheck, lint and tests pass for any code change.

## Provenance
Found by: bm-wp-117-9vy.2 orchestration acceptance run 4, F-8a (evidence ~/bm-acceptance/20260915/evidence-run4/F-8a/analysis.txt).
close_reason: Fixed in d754890 (A plugin agent.turn_ended hook sends a fixed stop notice to a stopped bm-worker's running bm-reviewer children; B worker.md/reviewer.md stop rules; E design §2.6 errata + Draft upstream request for a plugin agent cancel). Proof: npm test 1117 passed incl. plugin-stop-propagation (24) and bundle hook registration; typecheck/lint 0; CI 34993295765 success. Live F-8a re-run 5 on r5 payload: paseo stop on Worker 71476063 at 16:13:32Z while Reviewer 9b9ea3bb ran -> plugin sent the notice, Reviewer replied BM-REVIEW STOPPED and went idle ~4 s later (run 4: ~60 s, review completed); Worker woken once, cancelled nothing left, sent finished, asked the user, no further work; stop+120 s and +300 s 0 running, 0 new agents, git unchanged. Evidence ~/bm-acceptance/20260915/evidence-run5/F-8a/summary.txt. Known limitation (errata): interrupt via send, not a hard cancel, until Paseo offers a plugin cancel API.

comments.author: hieunguyentrung
comments.text: Investigation (Paseo 0.8 SDK + daemon, read-only): PARTIALLY SUPPORTED. Plugin can detect a canceled Worker turn via on('agent.turn_ended') outcome.kind='canceled' (lifecycle.d.ts), but PaseoAgentHandle has no cancel (only send/archive/...); cancelAgent exists only on the private DaemonClient; handle.send() to a running agent interrupts via replaceAgentRun but starts a new turn; archive is forbidden (ADR-005, REQ-026f). Cancel reason cannot distinguish user stop from message replace (re-read status: idle vs running). Paseo always sends a 'finished' notification to the parent when a child goes idle, so a stopped Worker is woken once. Options: A) plugin on turn_ended -> send a fixed stop notice to running bm-reviewer children (interrupt + one short turn; relies on reviewer.md); B) worker.md: when woken after a canceled turn, cancel_agent running Reviewers and send finished (real cancel but late); C) Reviewer polls parent (barred from Paseo tools); D) Manager-only (misses user stops); E) document as errata + README + upstream request for agent.cancel. Open design questions: does an interrupt + forced short reply count as 'stopped' under REQ-026f; stop notice wording; status re-read delay; what the woken Worker should do; log/error code; Manager stop same path; upstream ownership.

comments.author: hieunguyentrung
comments.text: Owner decision 2026-09-15: implement A + B + E. A = plugin hook on agent.turn_ended (canceled bm-worker, re-read status; if not running, send a fixed stop notice to running bm-reviewer children); B = worker.md rule: when woken after a canceled turn, cancel_agent any running Reviewers, send finished, do nothing else; reviewer.md recognises the stop notice; E = design errata + upstream request draft for a plugin agent.cancel. Then reinstall, re-run F-8a live, and uninstall/restore config at the end of acceptance.

comments.author: hieunguyentrung
comments.text: Implemented in d754890 (A plugin hook plugin/server/stop-propagation.ts registered from contribute; B worker.md group 6 + precedence 7 + Stop conditions, reviewer.md stop notice; E design §2.6 errata + docs/operations/paseo-upstream-request-agent-cancel.md Draft not sent). Local: build, typecheck, typecheck:plugin, lint exit 0; npm test 56 files / 1117 passed (plugin-stop-propagation 24 tests, bundle test registers agent.turn_ended). CI run 34993295765 success. Installed r5 tarball 16:10Z: plugin auto-reloaded (Plugin ready), payload has stop-propagation.ts, doctor exit 0. Live F-8a re-run (evidence-run5) in progress.

title: worker.md: Manager relay and peer finish notifications are read as a user Stop
description:
## Objective

`plugin/roles/worker.md` (Hard boundaries group 6) tells Worker to treat a turn
that "starts right after an interrupted turn — from a notification that a
Reviewer or another agent finished, or with no new instruction from the user" as
a stop. On a real daemon this matches Manager's ordinary behaviour, so Worker
halts mid-request when nothing stopped it.

## Steps to Reproduce

Observed five times during the WP-214 acceptance run (2026-09-16, real daemon,
`/tmp/bm-acc-20260916/repo`, Manager `06c0c92c`):

1. Send Manager a request; it delegates to a Worker.
2. While the Worker is working, send Manager any follow-up (in the run: a tier
   override). Manager relays it to the Worker with `send_agent_prompt`.
3. The Worker's turn is interrupted by the incoming message, so its next turn
   begins right after an interrupted turn.
4. The Worker reports `phase: finished` with `blockers: "STOPPED …"` and stops,
   with the request undelivered.

Also reproduced by a Reviewer finishing normally: the finish notification opens
the Worker's next turn, which the rule classifies as a stop, so the Worker does
not close the bead it had already implemented and reviewed.

Measured effect: request `req-20260916T064147Z` (one added docstring line)
needed four operator nudges to complete; three of the four stops happened when
the only remaining work was a single `br close` command. Request
`req-20260916T070544Z` stopped after 51k tokens, at the first step.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A message relayed by Manager, or a peer/sub-agent finish notification, does
  not by itself end the request: the Worker continues unless the message says it
  is stopping.
- A real user Stop (Paseo's Stop with no follow-up instruction) is still
  recognised and still triggers group 6 in full: cancel running Reviewers, touch
  nothing else, send `finished`.
- The distinction is stated in `worker.md` in a way that does not depend on
  wording of the incoming message alone.
- A test covers both directions: a relayed instruction continues the work, a
  bare interruption stops it.

## Notes

Out of scope for WP-214: this is the orchestration loop (`roles/worker.md`), not
the Dashboard, and the stop rule is product behaviour the owner approved. Raised
for the owner to decide rather than changed unilaterally.

The Dashboard is what surfaced it: the state column plus the workflow-step table
showed a request reported "finished" whose bead was never closed.

## Provenance

Found by the WP-214 Dashboard acceptance run; recorded in
`docs/operations/paseo-bm-dashboard-run-20260916.md` §3c "Phát hiện 2".
Not split from another bead.
close_reason: Fixed in plugin/roles/worker.md group 6: stop recognition is now a four-row table decided by what the turn brought — a stop message or an empty resume after a cut-off turn is a stop; an instruction (including one Manager relayed, a correction, a tier override or an answer to Worker's own question) and a bare peer finish notification are explicitly NOT stops. The Stop-conditions list and the finish-notification paragraph were made consistent, and the evidence (one real request halted five times, three of them with a single br close left) is kept beside the rule so it is not reasoned away. Verified: worker-instructions.ts regenerated by npm run build; test/roles-content-worker-implement.test.ts has a new bm-wqu case asserting the table order, the two not-a-stop rows and the Manager-relay rationale, plus the updated bm-wq6 cases; npm run typecheck, npm run lint and npm test all clean (1598 passing). Found by the WP-214 acceptance run and recorded in docs/operations/paseo-bm-dashboard-run-20260916.md section 3c.

title: install --help says preview only without --apply, but on a terminal install asks to apply and writes
description:
## Objective
The install help text describes what install actually does without --apply, so a user reading --help is not surprised.

## Context
Found while writing the README (bm-wp-118-4s4.1): install --help prints 'preview only without --apply', but src/commands/install/index.ts computes mayApply = flags.apply || interactive, so on a terminal install shows the plan, asks 'Apply these changes?' and writes on yes. This terminal behaviour is the designed and accepted flow (Phase 1a acceptance M-1: interactive install asks the confirmations). Without a terminal and without --apply it previews and exits 6. The help text is the part that is wrong.

## Scope
- Change the install help/usage text (and uninstall's if it has the same wording and the same behaviour) to say: without --apply, a terminal run shows the plan and asks before writing; a run without a terminal only previews (exit 6).
- Update any test that snapshots the help text.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run npx paseo-bm install --help: it says preview only without --apply.
2. Run npx paseo-bm install on a terminal without --apply.
3. Result: it asks 'Apply these changes?' and writes on yes; expected: the help text matches this.

## Acceptance Criteria
- install --help (and uninstall --help if affected) describes the terminal and no-terminal behaviour without --apply correctly.
- npm run build, typecheck, lint and tests pass.

## Provenance
Found by: bm-wp-118-4s4.1 README work (G-1), 2026-09-15.
close_reason: Fixed in 17f67fc: src/flags.ts install summary now reads 'without --apply: asks before writing on a terminal, preview only otherwise' (matches mayApply = flags.apply || interactive in src/commands/install/index.ts; behaviour unchanged as accepted in Phase 1a M-1). uninstall keeps 'preview only without --apply' because src/commands/uninstall.ts returns the preview when !options.apply. No test pins the text; node dist/index.js --help shows the new line; build, typecheck, typecheck:plugin, lint exit 0; npm test all passed.

title: README: hướng dẫn cài đặt đúng cho một CLI chạy bằng npx, không phải npm i
description:
## Objective
Người đọc README biết ngay paseo-bm là CLI chạy một lần bằng npx, và không cài nhầm bằng npm i.

## Context
Trang npmjs.com tự sinh ô 'npm i paseo-bm' cho mọi gói, không đọc README và không tuỳ chỉnh được. Với paseo-bm thì lệnh đó sai mục đích: metadata gói có bin paseo-bm -> dist/index.js và main rỗng, nên không có gì để import. Owner đã gặp đúng lỗi này: chạy npm i paseo-bm trong repo khiến dự án tự thêm chính nó vào dependencies. Ngoài ra README đang dẫn npx paseo-bm@next vì lúc viết chưa publish; sau khi phát hành, dist-tag latest cũng trỏ 0.1.0-alpha.0 nên npx paseo-bm cho kết quả như nhau.

## Scope
- README.md: mục Install dẫn thẳng npx paseo-bm, giữ @next như ghi chú để ghim prerelease khi đã có bản ổn định.
- Thêm một dòng ngay đầu README: đây là CLI chạy bằng npx, không cài bằng npm i vào dự án, và nói rõ ô lệnh trên trang npm là mặc định của npm.
- Không đổi package.json, không đổi dist-tag.

## Acceptance Criteria
- README nêu rõ cách chạy đúng và cảnh báo không dùng npm i.
- Mọi lệnh trong README khớp thực tế registry hiện tại (latest và next đều trỏ 0.1.0-alpha.0).
- npm run build, lint và test xanh.

## Provenance
Source: câu hỏi của owner 2026-09-16 sau khi phát hành.
close_reason: Fixed in bd62fda: README now opens with a note that paseo-bm is a CLI run once with npx, exports nothing to import, and that the 'npm i paseo-bm' box on npmjs.com is generated automatically for every package (verified from the registry metadata: bin paseo-bm -> dist/index.js, main null, type module). Install section leads with 'npx paseo-bm' and explains that npx leaves nothing behind; @next kept as the way to pin prereleases once a stable release exists. Removed the two 'npx paseo-bm@latest' references (Updating, E_RECORD_SCHEMA_TOO_NEW) because latest currently resolves to the 0.1.0-alpha.0 prerelease. Every other npx line in the README is a subcommand (install/doctor/uninstall) and was already correct. npm run lint exit 0, npm test 1117 passed.

title: CLI skills lỗi 127 vì thừa hưởng npm_config_package từ npx của paseo-bm
description:
## Objective
Khi chạy hộ npx -y skills add, tiến trình con không được thừa hưởng biến môi trường npm của lệnh npx đang chạy paseo-bm, để npx bên trong tải đúng gói skills.

## Context
Nghiệm thu Phase 1a 2026-09-15: paseo-bm chạy qua npx --package <tarball> truyền npm_config_package=<tarball> (đã kiểm), npm_command=exec, npm_lifecycle_event=npx... xuống tiến trình con; npx -y skills add bên trong đọc npm_config_package nên tìm lệnh skills trong gói paseo-bm -> 'sh: skills: command not found', mã 127, không cài được skills (M-9). Test giả lập dùng npx giả nên không bắt được.

## Scope
In scope:
- Dựng env cho tiến trình con skills: bỏ npm_config_package và các biến ngữ cảnh npm exec/lifecycle (npm_command, npm_lifecycle_event, npm_lifecycle_script, npm_config_call), giữ PATH và phần còn lại
- Test: env của tiến trình con không có các biến đó khi môi trường cha có
Out of scope:
- Đổi argv đã chốt

## Components Touched

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- Không

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Không đọc hay in giá trị biến môi trường khác.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Chạy paseo-bm qua npx --yes --package <tarball> paseo-bm install trên HOME tạm, đồng ý cài skills.
2. Kết quả: 'sh: skills: command not found', mã 127, assistOutcome failed; mong đợi CLI skills chạy thật.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Kiểm tay (ghi vào close reason): npx --package <tarball mới> paseo-bm install --install-skills trên HOME tạm chạy được CLI skills (mã khác 127)

## Primary Proof
npm test -- skills-assist

## Reversibility
Revert commit.

## Provenance
Source: nghiệm thu Phase 1a 2026-09-15 (bm-wp-120-b2e.1.2), evidence install-rerun.log
Requirements: REQ-007(e), M-9
close_reason: Fixed src/skills/assist.ts: runSkillsCommand spawns with skillsChildEnv(env), a copy of the environment without npm_config_package, npm_config_call, npm_command, npm_lifecycle_event and npm_lifecycle_script (argv and shell:false unchanged; other npm_config_* such as registry/proxy kept). Proof: npx vitest run test/skills-assist.test.ts -> 15 passed incl. a unit test of skillsChildEnv and an integration test where install --apply --json --install-skills runs with those variables set and the fake npx sees none of them while still seeing PATH and npm_config_registry; removing the fix makes the integration test fail.
